Title: Anwar ranked 13th among world's 500 most influential Muslims
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has been ranked 13th in the 2027 edition of The Muslim 500: The World's 500 Most Influential Muslims, published by the Jordan-based Royal Islamic Strategic Studies Centre (RISSC).
According to the 18th annual edition accessible at https://themuslim500.com, the publication noted that Anwar assumed office as Malaysia's 10th prime minister in November 2022, leading the unity government under the Pakatan Harapan coalition.
The report highlighted that Anwar, who is also finance minister, prioritised a digital and economic transition strategy under his Malaysia Madani framework, placing artificial intelligence, semiconductors, data centres, quantum computing and the energy transition at the heart of his government's agenda.
"In June 2026, Anwar highlighted the energy transition as a key pillar of Malaysia's development agenda, connecting the country's future energy needs directly to the rapid expansion of its high-tech infrastructure sectors," it said.
Regionally, the publication underscored Anwar's role as a constructive peace broker in Southeast Asia, notably his diplomatic initiatives to ease tensions and build trust between Thailand and Cambodia following border clashes in July 2025.
"As Malaysia's Prime Minister and Asean Chair, he hosted talks between the two countries' leaders in Putrajaya that helped secure a ceasefire. Anwar helped build trust between Bangkok and Phnom Penh, reinforcing Malaysia's image as a constructive peace broker in Southeast Asia," the report said.
The Muslim 500 also recognised Anwar as one of the world's most outspoken heads of state on the Palestinian cause, maintaining strong support for civilian protection and humanitarian access in Gaza.
"Taking an aggressive international stance, Anwar announced to the Malaysian Parliament that the country is spearheading a core international coalition drafting a formal resolution to expel Israel from the United Nations. Anwar reiterated that Malaysia's absolute non-recognition of Israel is permanent," it said.
According to the publication, Anwar's meetings with Hamas officials, including its late leader Ismail Haniyeh, drew public pushback from Western countries, though he dismissed the criticism and asserted Malaysia's sovereign right to determine its own foreign policy.
Beyond his political leadership, the citation traced Anwar's early activism as founder and president of the Malaysian Islamic Youth Movement (Abim) in 1971, as well as his career in major cabinet portfolios, including deputy prime minister and finance minister, during the 1990s.
It also highlighted his academic contributions, noting his visiting positions at St Antony's College, Oxford, Johns Hopkins University and Georgetown University.
"He is a co-founder of the International Institute of Islamic Thought (IIIT) established in the United States in 1981. Furthermore, he served as the Chancellor of the International Islamic University Malaysia (IIUM) from 1983 to 1988, and has received numerous international honorary degrees," it said.
In the 2027 edition, the top spot is jointly held by Saudi Arabia's King Salman bin Abdul-Aziz Al-Saud and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Pakistan's Prime Minister Mian Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif and Chief of Army Staff General Syed Asim Munir, alongside Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan.
Other prominent Southeast Asian figures in the Top 50 include Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto at 16th place, Nahdlatul Ulama chairman Yahya Cholil Staquf (21st) and Indonesian scholar Habib Luthfi bin Yahya (31st).
Meanwhile, Palestinian paediatrician and Kamal Adwan Hospital director Dr Hussam Abu Safiya, held in Israeli detention without charge since December 2024, was named The Muslim 500's Man of the Year for 2027 and ranked 50th.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar: 'You don't condemn those who "sakau", yet still kiss their hands'
Article:
ALOR GAJAH: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today questioned why some people continued to defend and honour leaders accused of plundering public funds, even as the government bore the cost of their past financial mismanagement.
He said corruption and abuse of power should not be excused because of a leader's political influence or race.
"You don't get angry with those who 'sakau'? You even kiss their hands and accept their donations.
"That makes me wonder what is happening to our country," he said at the Pesta Melaka, Rumah Kita programme at Taman Melaka Perdana here last night.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, cited the government's financial obligations involving Felda, 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) and Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH).
"Imagine this. I am now the finance minister and prime minister. Every year, RM1 billion is used to settle Felda's debts. Another RM2 billion to RM3 billion goes towards settling 1MDB's debts, while Tabung Haji requires another RM1 billion," he said.
He stressed that the fight against corruption must continue regardless of a person's position, race or political connections.
He said leaders entrusted with public office should prioritise the people's welfare instead of using their positions to amass personal wealth.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar: The problem is leaders without principles, not DAP
Article:
ALOR GAJAH: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said DAP was not the problem in the country's political landscape, but the lack of Malay leaders with principles and integrity.
He said leaders should be judged by their character, honesty and ability to serve the people, rather than their race.
"Our problem is not about the Chinese or Malays. It is about ensuring that we have Malay leaders with principles.
"Surely there are such leaders. There are many in Melaka, including young people. Choose those who are good, clean and have values. Don't let them grab everything for themselves once they get a little power," he said.
He was speaking at the Pesta Melaka, Rumah Kita programme at Taman Melaka Perdana here today.
Also present were Pakatan Harapan secretary-general Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail, PKR Wanita chief Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek and Amanah vice-president Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad.
Anwar, who is also PH chairman, said cooperation among different communities was important to ensure national stability, but this did not mean that political principles or the interests of the Malay community should be sidelined.
He said voters should assess leaders based on their track records and credibility, rather than be swayed by racial sentiments exploited in political contests.
"So, what kind of Malay leaders should we choose? Is it simply because they are Malay, or because they have good character, principles, do not steal or abuse their position, and are not arrogant?" he said.
He also urged voters to give young leaders with integrity and the ability to lead a chance to shape the state's future.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nacsa on amber alert amid unverified cyberattack claims, says Fahmi
Article:
MELAKA: No particularly worrying cybersecurity incidents have been confirmed so far, based on daily reports from the National Cyber Security Agency (Nacsa), said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
He said Nacsa's readiness level is currently at amber alert, or moderate, following claims of cyberattacks circulating on social media recently.
Fahmi said Nacsa had looked into the claims of cyber intrusions but had yet to verify their authenticity.
"I receive daily reports from Nacsa and so far, the agency has not reported any particularly worrying incidents. However, Nacsa's readiness level is at what is known as amber alert, which indicates a moderate level of preparedness.
"So far, there have been claims of cyberattacks and intrusions, but Nacsa has informed me that there is no confirmation of the incidents being circulated on social media. Should anything happen, Nacsa would certainly be the official source of information. So far, there has been no such confirmation," he said.
Fahmi, who is also Pakatan Harapan communications director, said this during a walkabout with PH's Ayer Molek state seat candidate for the Melaka election, Muhammad Hakimin Mokhtar, at the Ayer Molek night market here today.
Also present was PKR Advisory Council chairman Datuk Seri Dr. Wan Azizah Wan Ismail.

Title: Nvidia shares tumble as CEO resigns, major indices mixed
Article:
NEW YORK: Nvidia shares sank early Thursday after Chief Executive Jensen Huang resigned from the AI giant following revelations he had an affair with a woman accused of spying for China.
Pressure building on Huang heightened further Wednesday after The New York Times reported that he had another affair with an Nvidia executive who worked under him. The company's pioneering semiconductor technology has been at the center of the artificial intelligence boom.
About 25 minutes into trading, the Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 0.1 percent at 52,518.60.
The broad-based S&P 500 lost 0.3 percent at 7,598.94, while the tech-rich Nasdaq Composite Index dropped 0.4 percent to 25,362.29.
Other AI stocks were mixed with so-called hyperscalers Alphabet and Microsoft higher and Oracle and CoreWeave dropping. AMD, considered a rival to Nvidia, rose about two percent.
After opening down more than 13 percent, Nvidia shares were later off 7.1 percent as the company announced a shakeup that had begun to look inevitable, appointing Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress to serve as interim CEO.
Some analysts said Huang's departure won't affect short-term AI projects already in the works.
"In the near term, I think Nvidia will continue to perform as usual," said Ryuta Makino, software and semiconductor analyst at Gabelli Funds.
"The fundamentals won't change for calendar year 2027 and potentially calendar year 2028. A lot of these deals and supply chain are already locked up."
But Makino said Nvidia "will likely lose market share" over the longer term, affecting 2029 and beyond.
Adam Sarhan of 50 Park Investments noted that the Nvidia scandal comes amid a period of weakness in AI stocks due in part to worries about overbuilding capacity and exacerbated by US elections that showcased public hostility to data center.
On Nvidia, "we don't know the extent of the line that was crossed," said Sarha, adding that it is unknown whether Jensen Huang was "complicit" in any sharing of secrets with China.
"Why would I invest more in AI until we figure out what's going on?" Sarhan said. — AFP

Title: Trump calls for Apple ex-CEO Tim Cook to replace Huang at Nvidia
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said Thursday that former Apple CEO Tim Cook should replace Jensen Huang at Nvidia, after Huang quit over revelations of two affairs including one with an alleged Chinese spy.
"Now that Nvidia CEO JENSEN HUANG, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place – TIM COOK of Apple. A Legend replaces a Legend!" Trump, who was close to Huang, said on his Truth Social network. — AFP

Title: Loke maintains decision to resign despite Anwar's call for talks
Article:
MELAKA: DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke is standing by his decision to resign as transport minister despite Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's call for further discussions on the matter.
However, Loke gave his assurance that neither he nor his party was withdrawing support for Anwar's leadership.
Loke said his resignation was intended to reaffirm DAP's position against former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak being allowed to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest.
He stressed that all 40 DAP members of Parliament remained firmly behind Anwar despite his decision to leave the cabinet.
"I have submitted my resignation letter as a cabinet member to express my party's stand on Najib's house arrest.
"I resigned as a minister, but I am not withdrawing my support for Anwar.
"DAP and I remain committed to supporting Anwar as prime minister. This is something I want to make absolutely clear," he said at Pakatan Harapan's grand finale rally here tonight.
Loke was speaking shortly after Anwar told the gathering that
he had yet to receive the DAP leader's resignation
letter and wanted further discussions with him on the matter.
It was previously reported that Loke had announced his
immediate resignation
following Tuesday's High Court decision allowing Najib to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest.
It was reported recently that Loke had announced his immediate resignation following Tuesday's High Court decision allowing Najib to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest.
He said his decision was in line with a pledge he had made nearly seven weeks earlier to resign immediately if Najib was granted house arrest.
"I had already announced almost seven weeks ago that if Najib returned home, I would not wait even a minute. My resignation would take effect immediately.
"When I say I will do something, I will do it," he said.
He also rejected allegations by Barisan Nasional deputy chairman Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan that his resignation amounted to disrespect towards the Yang di-Pertuan Agong.
Loke said his decision was directed at Najib and should not be misconstrued as a challenge to the constitutional monarchy.
"This is not about disrespecting the Yang di-Pertuan Agong. We respect the powers of the King.
"This is our stand against Najib. It is about Najib, not the King," he said.

Title: Binance heist reveals uphill battle against hackers
Article:
An elite North Korean hacking group's US$6.3 billion theft from Binance is renewing scrutiny of a longstanding weakness in the cryptocurrency industry: hackers may need to compromise only one employee to get inside, while inconsistent security practices can allow them to turn that foothold into a massive theft.
The Oct 29 heist, described by experts as the largest cryptocurrency theft ever, unfolded in a matter of minutes after months of planning and preparation, according to Binance's initial investigation.
Cybersecurity experts said the attack raises questions not only about how exchanges defend employees against sophisticated social engineering, but also about whether they have adequate internal controls to limit what an attacker can do once an employee's computer or credentials are compromised.
Social engineering is a well-understood threat in the industry, said Jonathan Alexander, chief technology officer of S&P Global's OpenZeppelin, a blockchain security provider.
The bigger question, he said, is why exchanges do not have stronger internal safeguards and circuit breakers to prevent an attacker who breaches an engineer's computer —like what happened at Binance — from escalating access and moving assets.
Varying cybersecurity practices across the industry compound the problem, said Alexander, along with a longstanding aversion among some cryptocurrency advocates to controls they view as inconsistent with blockchain's decentralised ethos that sometimes views things such as limits on transaction amounts and automatic reviews of patterns of spending as infringing on inherent privacy rights.
"I think that falsely, that has led some people to think that things like circuit breakers, things like more controls on the accounts, would be unacceptable or would be absolutely in conflict with that need to avoid censorship," Alexander added.
"In my view, you can have security controls and have protections against that."
The Binance attack is the latest in a string of major cryptocurrency hacks that have resulted in more than US$22.3 billion in stolen funds since 2021, according to blockchain intelligence firm Chainalysis.
The scale of the losses has intensified debate over whether exchanges need more consistent standards governing access, transaction controls and other defences.
"I do expect we'll see more clarity and standardisation in the kind of cybersecurity expectations and, hopefully, requirements for investor protection and trust," said Alexander. "These things show why it has to change."
Cryptocurrency exchanges present unusually attractive targets because hackers can identify wallets holding enormous sums of readily transferable digital assets and, in some cases, the employees with access to the systems controlling them.
That has made engineers and tech workers prime targets for elaborate social-engineering operations.
Alex Pruden, chief executive officer of blockchain and digital-asset security firm Project Eleven, said defenders face a fundamental disadvantage against attackers who need to succeed only once.
"The best practices in cybersecurity that we've had up to this point are just simply not up to the task of the world that we live in, in terms of what the threat is."
Pruden expects the Binance theft to spur greater investment in cybersecurity, including safeguards around internal artificial intelligence tools and agents that could themselves expand an attacker's capabilities if compromised.
"We're at the beginning of the beginning of that story, but I just think like the Binance hack showed, those tools can be turned against you very, very quickly and they can be very hard to undo the damage once it's done."
Cryptocurrency exchanges have already begun moving to bolster defences and increase information sharing following the Binance hack, Reuters reported on Oct 30.
The uneven security practices identified by experts are mirrored by a fragmented US regulatory system.
Unlike banks, US cryptocurrency exchanges do not operate under a single federal cybersecurity regime. Instead, requirements vary depending on where companies operate and which state licences they hold.
New York imposes some of the industry's toughest requirements.
Elsewhere, crypto companies may be subject primarily to state money-transmitter rules.
Many exchanges do not operate in the US and are not subject to those state oversight regimes, although they may operate under separate requirements wherever they do business.
The writers are from Reuters

Title: Trump's pause on Iran conflict is as costly as new strikes
Article:
AS United States President Donald Trump weighs his next steps in the Iran war, Gulf energy producers have adapted to a no-war, no-peace reality that is making their operations more expensive and risky.
Even without renewed fullscale fighting, those additional costs could help put a floor under global oil prices.
The question is how long this uneasy equilibrium can last.
But the US military continues to build up forces in the Middle East. Mediation efforts led by Qatar and Pakistan also continue, though Washington and Teheran appear far apart on some of the thorniest issues, particularly Iran's nuclear programme.
This suggests Trump's current moratorium on major strikes may not signal an imminent end to the conflict.
It may instead be a tactical pause as Trump considers whether another round of air strikes can improve Washington's hand in seeking a favourable deal to end a war now in its ninth month.
Low-intensity conflict is becoming the Middle East's new normal even as the region's crude exports recover.
Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has averaged 10.5 million barrels per day (bpd) since the start of last month, according to Kpler.
While that is still below the prewar average of 13.5 million bpd, it is up substantially from the depths of the disruption.
Moreover, once alternative routes bypassing Hormuz are included, total average Gulf crude exports have risen to 16.7 million bpd since early last month, just shy of the pre-war level of 17 million bpd.
But this obscures an important distinction: the risk of another full-scale war has declined, but the cost of living with the existing conflict has not.
Iranian attacks on vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz have become an almost daily occurrence.
The International Maritime Organisation tracked 131 confirmed incidents near the narrow waterway from the start of the war on Feb 28 through Nov 9.
The number rose sharply to 35 last month, the highest monthly total during the conflict.
The real figure is likely higher because shipowners often choose not to report incidents that cause little or no damage.
Gulf oil and liquefied natural gas exporters have responded by sending tankers through Hormuz in convoys, using narrow routes close to Oman's coast under US Navy protection and conducting ship-to-ship transfers to limit the exposure of any one ship.
While this complex process is working, it comes at a high price.
Freight and insurance costs remain about 10 times pre-war levels.
Unless Washington and Teheran reach a durable agreement, there is little reason to expect those costs to disappear.
Gulf producers are normalising the exceptional. While the new normal highlights the extraordinary resilience of the Gulf oil industry, it also emphasises the weakness of today's equilibrium.
For decades, a sustained disruption to shipping through Hormuz was treated as a remote but potentially catastrophic event.
Yet producers have shown that they can adapt with creative workarounds.
But adapting to a crisis is not the same as resolving it.
Iran has every incentive to continue attacking vessels crossing Hormuz. While the US blockade on Iran's oil exports is choking its economy, the government shows no sign that it is willing to compromise on its red lines.
Teheran likely believes it can outlast Washington, particularly after the Republican Party's drubbing last week.
That leaves Trump with an awkward choice.
The midterm elections sent a clear signal about the political cost of an unpopular war.
But is Washington willing to accept a deal that does little to curb Teheran's nuclear programme, reinforcing the idea that the US lost the war?
If no tangible diplomatic progress is made in the coming weeks, Trump could still conclude that renewed strikes offer the best chance of strengthening the US hand in negotiations.
However, unless military action delivers a decisive blow that significantly weakens the Iranian government, another round of fighting could actually harden Teheran's position and make a settlement more difficult.
The danger, therefore, is not simply another dramatic surge in oil prices caused by renewed war.
It is that the Middle East settles into something more durable and more insidious: a conflict intense enough to keep shipping dangerous, insurance expensive and energy infrastructure vulnerable, but contained enough for the world to learn to live with it.
The writer is from Reuters

Title: Man arrested with suspected syabu in Kudat
Article:
KUDAT: Police arrested a man after seizing nine packets of suspected syabu weighing 51.06g in Kampung Lodung, Kudat.
The man, in his 30s, tested positive for drugs and has six previous criminal records, including three related to offences under the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952.
Kudat district police chief Superintendent Mohd Haris Ibrahim said the suspect was arrested by a team from the district police headquarters' Narcotics Criminal Investigation Division at about 2pm.
Police also seized a transparent plastic container, a small black bag and a yellow transparent straw, which were believed to be linked to drug abuse.
"The drugs seized were estimated to be worth RM5,100," he said in a statement.
Haris said an initial urine screening test found that the suspect was positive for amphetamine and methamphetamine.
The drugs were believed to be intended for distribution.
The case is being investigated under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952. An application for a seven-day remand order had been made.

Title: NST Leader:Prioritising a healthy ageing reform agenda
Article:
The longest a human being has lived is 122 years while the average global life expectancy is 74 years.
Malaysia's is 74 to 77 years, the oldest ever recorded is 113 years. In striving for a long life, the salutation "semoga panjang umur" (may you live long) is imbued in prayers and birthday wishes.
The real objective is good mental and physical health, and reliable financial means for sustenance, medical emergencies and leisurely pursuits.
The concern was expressed by Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah, who affirmed that healthy ageing should not be a privilege reserved only for those who can afford it.
In delivering his royal address at a wellness forum, the Sultan of Perak asserted that healthy ageing must be inclusive, accessible through environment, services and technology.
Sultan Nazrin has compelled us to do a rethink on what it means to live longer. We must reconfigure retirement and pension systems, lifetime education, employment opportunities, healthcare financing, wealth distribution and inter-generational wealth transfers.
It doesn't just mean avoiding illness or maintaining a strong physique: it also means an active, meaningful and independent life for the duration of our lives.
Malaysia is on the right path with the National Policy for Older Persons: elderly and preventive healthcare, senior citizen centres and chronic disease management.
In doing so, the plan is to combat ageism and discrimination, create age-friendly communities, provide integrated and long-term healthcare.
As leading examples, healthy ageing in Japan and Singapore are national priorities, something Malaysia is inadequately prepared for.
Here's what is needed: a national strategy combining retirement income, health and long-term care, housing and social protection because in 2036, Malaysia becomes an ageing nation when 15 per cent of the population is 60 and above.
With more people retiring, medical services spike and the elderly need extra help with daily activities. Pension and retirement savings will face increasing pressure.
For now, only 15 per cent of seniors age healthily, based on daily routine, cognitive health, social support and absence of chronic diseases.
Malaysia may need investments of RM10 to RM15 billion annually to establish a comprehensive national healthy-ageing programme until 2031.
Funding goes to demands for elderly care, trained caregivers and affordable long-term care facilities on top of equitable access to rural communities and lower-income families.
Employers, local authorities, communities and families have to step up with practical policies, adequate funding and accessible services.
We can't wait for the aged nation fallout: healthy ageing is not measured by longevity but by the quality of our remaining years.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police to send team to Pakistan over 130 Malaysians detained in scam raid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police will send officers to Pakistan to investigate the detention of 130 Malaysians in a raid on a suspected scam centre in Rawalpindi last month.
Commercial Crime Investigation Department (CCID) director Datuk Rusdi Mohd Isa said the officers would meet Pakistani authorities, record statements and examine devices seized during the raid.
He said examining the evidence was important to uncover the syndicate's modus operandi, including its alleged use of Royal Malaysia Police uniforms to deceive victims.
"We need to arrange a meeting to obtain statements from the authorities there, as well as examine the evidence and devices seized. We also want more information about the parties who brought them to Pakistan," he said at the CCID monthly press conference at Bukit Aman.
Rusdi said police received information about the detention at the end of October through official channels involving the Home Ministry and their Pakistani counterparts, although the arrests were made on Oct 13.
The identities of all 130 Malaysians were subsequently confirmed through cooperation between the police, embassies and Interpol.
He said 59 of those detained were from Sabah and 57 from Sarawak, with the rest from Johor, Selangor, Kuala Lumpur and Kelantan. Checks found that 92 had no criminal records in Malaysia, while the others had records involving various offences, including drugs, fraud and gambling. Two were wanted in connection with fraud cases in Sabah.
On their immigration status, 107 had overstayed their visas, 20 had valid visas, two had visa extensions and one had no valid travel documents. The Malaysians arrived in Pakistan in stages between June 8 and Sept 29, with the highest number, 53, arriving on Aug 3.
Addressing claims that they had been deceived by job offers, Rusdi said investigative experience showed that some people taken overseas to work for scam syndicates might have known the real purpose of their recruitment.
"However, based on investigative experience, there are individuals who are believed to know the true purpose of being taken abroad to work for a scam syndicate, but play different roles such as call operators, cooks or supervisors," he said.
Pakistani media previously reported that the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency raided premises at Kasa Tower, Bahria Town Phase VIII, Rawalpindi, allegedly used as a call centre for financial scams targeting Malaysians.
The syndicate
reportedly impersonated
bank customer service officers and police, using false allegations of money laundering to deceive victims. -- BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Azalina: Malaysian Bar has right to challenge Najib house arrest decision
Article:
BANGI: The Malaysian Bar has the right to challenge the Federal Territories Pardons Board's decision allowing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest, said Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.
She said the Bar is entitled to mount such a challenge if it believes it has grounds to question the decision.
"But I have always stressed that when we speak of matters under Article 42, it is considered what is referred to as the prerogative of mercy, which we know is among the powers fully vested in the discretion of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, the power of pardon.
"So it is up to the Malaysian Bar as to what it wants to bring... If the Malaysian Bar feels it has the right to question any issue, that is its right," she told reporters here today after a certificate presentation ceremony for the Professional Mediation Certification Course and Mediator Appointment Certificates, and the launch of the Legal Aid Department's 2026 Madani Mediation Centre Handbook.
Earlier today, the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) objected to the Malaysian Bar's bid to challenge the Pardons Board's decision concerning Najib's SRC International Sdn Bhd sentence.
Senior federal counsel Ahmad Hanir Hambaly@Arwi told High Court Judge S. Indra Nehru that the A-GC had received the Bar's application for leave to commence judicial review by email two days ago and needed time to file written submissions.
Meanwhile, Najib's lawyer Muhammad Farhan Muhammad Shafee told the court that his client also intended to file written submissions, as any decision after leave is granted could affect him.
Lawyer Zainur Zakaria, representing the Malaysian Bar, did not object to the requests by the A-GC and Najib's lawyers.
Judge Indra Nehru fixed March 17 next year to hear the application and ordered written submissions to be filed by Dec 14, with replies due on or before Dec 28.
On Nov 10, the Bar filed the judicial review application naming the Federal Territories Pardons Board, the Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform), the Director-General of Prisons and Najib as respondents.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Singapore barred Alice Huang from re-entry following investigation
Article:
SINGAPORE: Alice Huang, the alleged Chinese spy at the heart of a scandal at chipmaker Nvidia , left Singapore in February and was barred from re-entering following an investigation into possible offences, Singapore's home affairs ministry said on Thursday.
Nvidia said on Thursday that its chief executive officer Jensen Huang is stepping down, as pressure has mounted on him in recent days after reports said the 63-year-old, who is married, had an affair with Alice Huang, whom US authorities suspect of spying for Beijing.
The ministry said Alice Huang, a former executive at Nvidia customer Megaspeed, was investigated for possible offences including buying servers that were exported via Singapore to Malaysia without entering the Singapore market.
She was investigated "for suspected involvement in the possible offences in Singapore, given her position as then-CEO, chairperson, and one of the key controllers of Megaspeed," the ministry said in a statement. It said the investigation did not concern espionage.
The ministry said there was insufficient evidence to establish that Alice Huang had committed any offences, but it said she had provided police with "information, which she knew to be inaccurate" during the investigation and had downplayed her role in Megaspeed.
She was issued a stern warning and barred from re-entering the country, it said.

Title: Melaka poised to become national esports training hub
Article:
JASIN: Melaka could become the country's national esports training hub, with Majlis Amanah Rakyat (Mara) Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) institutions in the state set to be developed into a centre to nurture professional players.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the proposal had received Mara chairman Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki's backing following its announcement at the Jelajah E-Sports Melaka Biru 2026 programme in Duyong two days ago.
He said the centre would serve as an important platform for developing local esports talent, particularly among the younger generation.
"I would like to confirm that the Mara chairman has agreed to turn Mara's TVET institutions in Melaka into a national esports training centre," he said when officiating the Jelajah E-Sports Melaka Biru 2028 programme in Bandar Merlimau here.
Zahid, who is also BN chairman, said he wanted Melaka to host a world-level esports championship in 2028.
He said the proposal followed discussions with the president of the World Esports organisation, who had expressed interest in holding the championship in Malaysia.
He said Melaka should be given priority over other states as the host venue, giving the state an opportunity to become a focal point for the international esports community.
"I do not want this championship to be held in Kuala Lumpur, Penang or Johor. Instead, I want it to be held in Melaka in 2028," he said.
Zahid said he would hold further discussions with caretaker Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh on the proposal.
He hoped the state government would support the event, including by providing full sponsorship if Melaka was selected as the host.
He added that esports development in Melaka should be strengthened to produce teams capable of winning not only at state level but also in national and international competitions.
"We want to see a team from Merlimau emerge as state champions before going on to challenge for the national title.
"We are proud of our national teams that have won at the world level. We hope Malaysian esports teams, including HomeBois and Selangor Red Giants (SRG), will emerge as world champions and bring glory to the country," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ex-UKMShape director charged with money laundering
Article:
SHAH ALAM: A former director of Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia's (UKM) UKMShape has been charged with 21 counts of money laundering involving more than RM1.55 million.
Datuk Muhammad Husin, 64, pleaded not guilty to all the charges before Sessions Court judge Awang Kerisnada Awang Mahmud today.
The charges allege that Husin was involved in 21 money-laundering transactions totalling RM1,552,645.69 between 2022 and 2026.
The money was allegedly derived from an offence involving the use of his position as UKMShape director for personal benefit, including the purchase of personal assets.
The underlying offence is linked to Section 23(1) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Act 2009.
All 21 money-laundering charges were brought under Section 4(1)(b) of the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001 (AMLATFPUAA).
Deputy public prosecutor Muaz Ahmad Khairuddin conducted the prosecution, while Husin was represented by lawyer Adam Danial.
The court took note of the RM80,000 bail and additional conditions imposed earlier. The case was fixed for mention on Dec 14.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar: No one defied King's decree over Najib's house arrest
Article:
AYER MOLEK: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has denied claims that he and the government defied the Yang di-Pertuan Agong over the house arrest of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak.
He said his relationship with His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia remained cordial, adding that the decision on Najib's house arrest was not within his authority.
"Certain leaders are claiming that we have defied the King. I am the prime minister, and the King called me this evening. Our relationship is good.
"His Majesty has seen that Najib has been in prison for four years and wants to grant him house arrest. But that is not within my power. My responsibility is to follow the law," he said.
The Pakatan Harapan chairman said there was also no question of the attorney-general defying the King's decree, as the latter was merely following the legal process.
"Who has defied the decree? The attorney-general takes time because he is responsible for upholding the law. When the King issued the decree for Najib's release, the attorney-general agreed.
"But we have to follow the process and bring the matter to court for a decision on when it can be implemented. That is all," he said.
Anwar was speaking at a session with Ayer Molek PH candidate Muhammad Hakimin Mokhtar.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Husband and wife found dead in embrace in Papar sewage pond
Article:
PAPAR: A husband and wife were found dead in a sewage pond at a pig farm in Kampung Kawari, Papar.
They were found in an embrace. Police believe the 52-year-old man slipped into the pond and his 50-year-old wife fell in while trying to save him.
Both were Indonesian citizens working at the farm.
Papar district police chief Superintendent Heryan Mohd Tahir said police received information from a member of the public about the discovery at 11.56am.
He said a team from the Papar police station and the Fire and Rescue Department was sent to the scene.
"Initial investigations found that the male victim is believed to have slipped and fallen into the sewage pond, while his wife is believed to have tried to help him but also fell in," he said when contacted today.
Heryan said the circumstances surrounding the incident were still under investigation.
The bodies were sent to the forensic unit at Papar Hospital.
He said the case had been classified as a sudden death report.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to step down in big blow to AI boom
Article:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is stepping down, leaving the AI industry without its biggest champion and clouding the future of the chipmaker he built into an AI powerhouse.
Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will take over as interim CEO as Nvidia looks for a permanent successor, the company said on Thursday. It named former Synopsys CEO and board member Harvey Jones as its first-ever board chairman.
Huang, who co-founded Nvidia and is its fourth-largest investor with a stake of about 3.61 per cent, will exit the board as well.
Nvidia shares fell more than 10 per cent in premarket trading, and weighed on the broader market.
Pressure had been mounting on Huang in recent days after reports said the 63-year-old, who is married, had an affair with a Chinese businesswoman who US authorities suspect of spying for Beijing.
Nvidia's board met on Wednesday to consider his ouster, a person familiar with the matter said, after reports earlier in the day that Huang also had an extramarital affair with a senior company executive who reported to him.
Huang's exit plunges the US$4 trillion company into uncertainty and threatens to disrupt an AI ecosystem that he helped bankroll by pouring Nvidia's swelling cash pile back into cloud providers, suppliers and the industry's biggest labs.
Investor sentiment toward AI stocks has already been shaky as soaring cash burn and rising debt at traditionally cash-rich tech giants fuel doubts over whether the AI boom will pay off.
The departure could also have far-reaching consequences for US chip export policy, given Huang's push to preserve access to the Chinese market and his close ties with US President Donald Trump.
Trump said on Sunday that Huang had "done an amazing job for our country" and that the Nvidia chief had told him he had no idea the Chinese woman he had an affair with was a spy.
HUANG'S ROCK-STAR STATUS
For years, Nvidia was best known to gamers chasing top-tier graphics. But its chips' ability to perform many calculations at once has made them the oil of the AI boom and a strategic prize in the US-China race to dominate the technology. It also made Nvidia the world's most valuable company.
That turned Huang into a rock-star CEO, mobbed by fans in Taiwan and South Korea who ask him to sign books, posters and sometimes even their bodies. Such is his pull that stocks moved at his mere mention of company names at events.
But scrutiny of his conduct has intensified in recent days after reports of his relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based cloud company Megaspeed who US authorities have concluded was a Chinese intelligence asset.
The two, who have been photographed together in Taiwan, Singapore and California, are not related.
Washington has also investigated Megaspeed, a coveted official Nvidia cloud partner with priority access to its chips, over suspicions it helped China obtain advanced AI chips restricted under US export controls, according to media reports. Beijing has denied Alice Huang is a spy.
Earlier this month, Nvidia's board launched a probe, led by independent directors with outside legal counsel, into whether Jensen Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. It also expressed confidence in him at the time.
The controversy escalated on Wednesday when the New York Times reported Jensen Huang also had an affair with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice-president of healthcare, who reported to him.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Anwar confirms he has yet to receive Loke's resignation letter
Article:
MELAKA: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim wants to hold further discussions with DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke over his resignation as transport minister.
Anwar said he had yet to receive Loke's resignation letter, despite the Seremban member of Parliament announcing his decision two days ago.
"I have not received Anthony Loke's resignation letter.
"If he wants to take a short break, that is fine. But if he wants to resign, we need to discuss the matter again," he said during Pakatan Harapan's grand finale rally here.
His statement was then followed shouts of agreement from supporters in the rally.
Loke had announced his immediate resignation following Tuesday's High Court decision allowing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest.
Anwar, who is also PH chairman, defended Loke's performance as transport minister, saying there was no reason for an honest, trustworthy and committed minister to step down.
He said Loke had introduced various proposals, projects and programmes to improve public transport services and make daily travel easier for Malaysians, including taxi drivers.
"When I praise him, those from Pas and Umno question why Anwar is praising DAP or the Chinese.
"But when we appoint a minister, what matters is whether that minister is trustworthy, clean and hardworking.
"He has contributed many ideas, projects and programmes to make travelling easier for the people, including taxi drivers.
"Yet, people like him are being told to resign, while those who are problematic are being asked to stay. The world has turned upside down," he said.
Anwar also described Loke as a close friend and one of the Cabinet ministers who had consistently demonstrated a strong work ethic.
He said Loke's leadership had earned the respect of civil servants, including Malay officers serving in the Transport Ministry.
"He is among the ministers who work very hard and have many ideas to help ordinary Malaysians, particularly in transportation.
"I have spoken to Malay officers in his ministry, and he is well received by them," he said.
Anwar also criticised attempts to judge political leaders based on their race or party affiliation rather than their integrity and ability to serve.
He said Malaysia needed leaders from all communities who were honest, competent and committed to protecting the people's interests.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Foreigner who severed cop's hand had expired passport - Immigration DG
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:  The 32-year-old foreigner who severed a policeman's hand in a parang attack in Kepong yesterday was in Malaysia illegally, with his passport having expired in 2020.
Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said the man had previously held a student pass from 2015 to 2018.
"His passport expired in 2020 and he was in the country illegally," he said when contacted today.
In the 7pm incident yesterday, Lance Corporal Thierry Rodger Pendy, 26, suffered a severed right hand after being
attacked by a man armed with two parangs
at an apartment in Desa Aman Puri, Kepong.
The suspect fled but was later tracked to a nearby playground, where he was shot dead after attacking another police officer with a parang while resisting arrest.
He was pronounced dead upon arrival at Selayang Hospital.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad today confirmed that the eight-hour surgery to
reattach
Thierry's hand at Kuala Lumpur Hospital was successful.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Unusual shellfish haul draws crowds to Pantai Sabak, Kelantan
Article:
KOTA BARU: Large numbers of shellfish believed to be pen shells have washed ashore at Pantai Sabak, drawing crowds of residents eager to collect them.
The shellfish were first spotted yesterday evening, with incoming waves bringing more towards the shore.
Pantai Sabak resident Nor Ain Mat, 33, said she was alerted to their appearance by her nephew, who visited the beach with several friends at 6pm.
She said she rushed to the beach and was surprised by the sight, having never encountered the species despite living near the coast for years.
After sharing a live video on TikTok, she received comments from viewers identifying the shellfish as kepah or kerang kapak, which they said were edible and could fetch high prices.
Nor Ain said large numbers continued to wash ashore with each incoming wave, prompting people to collect them in sacks and baskets. Some even filled the backs of their four-wheel-drive vehicles.
She managed to collect a sackful, keeping some to cook and selling the rest.
She said she had been told the shellfish could fetch RM2.50 each at restaurants, but was selling her collection for RM10 a kg.
Several buyers had already expressed interest in collecting their purchases, she added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Cops bust 112 scam syndicates, detain 932 in nationwide operation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police have busted 112 scam syndicates operating through call centres and detained 932 people in a nationwide operation conducted from Oct 19 to 31.
Bukit Aman Commercial Crime Investigation Department director Datuk Rusdi Mohd Isa said 153 raids were carried out during Op Magpie 01/2026, exceeding the initial target of 100.
He said police also conducted 650 proactive inspections of premises during the operation.
"Of the 932 people detained, 106 were Malaysians while 826 were foreigners. The arrests involved 796 men and 136 women.
"By nationality, Chinese nationals accounted for the highest number of arrests at 538, followed by Vietnam (93), Taiwan (40), Indonesia (36), Japan (21), Pakistan (18), Myanmar and the Philippines (14 each)," he told a press conference here today.
Rusdi said 106 of the 153 raids, or 69.28 per cent, were conducted at condominium residences, 34 at residential premises, eight at resorts or hotels and five at office buildings, shoplots and warehouses.
Initial analysis identified 136 records of scam modus operandi, with non-existent investment schemes and love scams accounting for 27 each, followed by phone scams (25), online gambling (16) and fake job offers (11).
The syndicates also targeted victims across national borders, with 130 of the 144 recorded target-country entries involving victims overseas and 14 in Malaysia.
China recorded the highest number of targets at 62, followed by the United States (12), Vietnam and Indonesia (seven each), and Japan and Hong Kong SAR (six each).
Police seized 2,058 mobile phones, 433 laptops or tablets, 161 computers or monitors, 112 routers or modems, 40 passports or visas and seven vehicles, along with various documents and equipment linked to the syndicates.
Cash amounting to RM102,635 was also seized.
Rusdi said 117 investigation papers were opened following the operation, with 70 still under investigation and 45 having reached the prosecution stage in court.
He said 809 of those arrested were identified as customer service personnel or operators, while another 70 were supervisors or team leaders.
Investigations were continuing to identify the syndicates' masterminds, operational coordinators and those responsible for managing their finances and providing facilities.
These efforts included digital forensic analysis, as well as examinations of communication records and financial transactions.
Police advised the public to beware of scams, protect their banking details and contact the NSRC on 997 if they suspected fraud.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: P.I.E net profits almost tripled in Q3
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: P.I.E. Industrial Bhd recorded RM11.52 million net profits for the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 (Q3 FY26), almost tripled a year ago when it reported RM4.49 million, on improved factory utilisation and tighter cost controls.
Revenue rose four per cent to RM212.48 million from RM204.90 million previously, mainly driven by stronger demand for raw wire and cable as well as wire harness products, which offset weaker revenue from its EMS segment.
For the nine months ended Sept 30, 2026, however, PIE Industrial's net profit fell to RM9.12 million from RM25.87 million in the corresponding period last year, while revenue declined 24 per cent to RM535.11 million from RM707.69 million.
The weaker cumulative performance was mainly attributable to lower demand for its EMS activities, which recorded a pre-tax loss of RM11.10 million during the period, compared with a pre-tax profit of RM9.66 million previously.
Looking ahead, the group expects its recovery momentum to continue into the fourth quarter, supported by stronger revenue growth and the gradual commencement of mass production for several artificial intelligence (AI) server-related products.
It said the new products are expected to contribute to higher fourth-quarter revenue and expand its overall business scale, as it seeks to capitalise on growing global demand for AI servers and the China+1 manufacturing diversification strategy.
For 2027 and beyond, PIE Industrial plans to increase its focus and investment in switch and AI server-related businesses, while exploring opportunities in emerging segments such as AI key components and robotics.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 149 Chinese citizens deported through Penang airport
Article:
SIK: A total of 149 Chinese undocumented migrants have been deported to their home country through Penang International Airport.
They were deported yesterday.
In a statement, the Kedah Immigration Department said all the detainees were men who had previously been held at the Belantik Immigration Depot in Sik.
The repatriation costs were fully borne by their families and employers.
The department said representatives from the Consulate-General of the People's Republic of China in Penang had also assisted with arrangements for the detainees' return.
"All the detainees had completed their sentences and undergone deportation proceedings in accordance with the Immigration Act 1959/63 (Act 155) and the Immigration Regulations 1963," it said.
The department said all those deported had also been blacklisted in the Immigration Department's system to prevent them from re-entering the country.

Title: Five things to know about Nvidia
Article:
NEW YORK: After launching as a small gaming start-up and morphing into the top chip designer for artificial intelligence, US tech giant Nvidia faces unprecedented turbulence after its co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang reportedly had a second extramarital affair with an employee.
Huang had already acknowledged being "unfaithful" to his wife, reportedly with a woman US intelligence officials believe was a spy for China.
Here are five things to know about the firm headquartered in Santa Clara, California, where the board is reportedly weighing Huang's future as chief executive.
TRANSFORMATIVE GPUs
Behind the acronym lies the driving force behind the new generation of artificial intelligence, particularly generative AI -- that is, a version capable of creating text, music, images or video based on a prompt couched in everyday language.
The graphics processing unit (GPU), also known as a graphics card, functions as a computing unit much faster and vastly more powerful than a conventional microprocessor (CPU).
It has become essential for managing user requests for generative AI in real time, as these require processing vast amounts of data.
According to the research firm TrendForce, ChatGPT requires around 30,000 GPUs to operate. Google, for its cloud computing business, is also a major consumer of Nvidia processors, as are Microsoft and Amazon Web Services.
EVIL EYE
Co-founded in 1993 by three former employees of major IT companies -- Jen-Hsun Huang (who now goes by Jensen), Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem -- the company took a while to decide on a name.
In a 2017 interview with US magazine Fortune, Huang explained that the name "Nvidia" comes from the letters N and V, which they used in their file names to stand for "Next Version."
They selected the Latin word "invidia," meaning envy or jealousy, as their company name, albeit omitting the initial "i".
"Invidia" can also be associated with the concept of the "evil eye," a curse cast via a single glance. That meaning is suggested in the company's logo, a stylized green and white eye.
VIDEO GAMES TO DATA CENTRES
After its launch, Nvidia became the first company entirely dedicated to graphics processors, hoping to ride the video games wave as they started to feature more sophisticated animation and 3D graphics.
Nvidia launched the world's first GPU back in 1999, and amid the internet revolution it developed processors tailored for data centre infrastructure that enabled companies and also individuals to access computing power previously the preserve of a handful of researchers and major technology firms.
RIVALS IN SLIPSTREAM
Nvidia's two main rivals in the graphics card market are the American companies AMD (Advanced Micro Devices) and Intel, both of whom boast longer histories.
According to Jon Peddie Research, Nvidia accounted for approximately 90 per cent of standalone GPUs shipped worldwide in the first quarter of this year.
Nvidia designs its chips but does not have its own manufacturing facilities, unlike AMD, making it a "fabless" company whose products are made by TSMC in Taiwan -- where Huang was born.
After briefly taking the top spot in 2024 as world's most valuable company by market capitalization, Nvidia has since vied for that honor with fellow US giants Apple and Microsoft.
It posted net profit of US$120 billion for its last fiscal year to January 25, 2026, as revenue reached a staggering US$216 billion.
Huang has said he sees annual revenue surging to US$1 trillion through 2027.
MAN IN BLACK
Huang, who has spent more than 33 of his 63 years as Nvidia's only CEO ever, has an atypical image of a boss with his dry humor and laid-back style.
Whereas Apple's Steve Jobs had his turtleneck, Huang's signature is the black leather jacket he often sports during Nvidia presentations.
Shortly after the company's founding, Huang turned down a contract with the video game console maker Sega to pivot toward a new processor capable of competing in the personal computer market, narrowly avoiding bankruptcy along the way in the mid-1990s.
In recent years, Huang has become one of the AI industry's most influential voices, strongly advocating for so-called "open" models that can be freely reused and modified -- including those from China.
He views such models as providing healthy competition to the closed models from OpenAI (ChatGPT) and Anthropic (Claude).
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: IOIPG Malaysia Reit's IPO saw 0.59 times oversubscription, offer price fixed lower
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The initial public offering (IPO) of IOI Properties Group Bhd's real estate investment trust (Reit), IOIPG Malaysia Reit, had been oversubscribed by 0.59 times for its public portion.
While the non-Bumiputera portion was oversubscribed by 1.85 times, the Bumiputera portion of the public issuance was undersubscribed. According to IOIPG Malaysia Reit, the Bumiputera's public portion was subscribed at 0.33 times.
The institutional offering was fully subscribed, drawing interest mainly from long-term investors, including government-linked investment companies (GLICs) and insurers.
The IPO price was fixed at 91 sen per unit following the bookbuilding process, down from the initial retail price of 96 sen.
At the final price, the offering is expected to raise about RM2 billion, while giving the Reit an expected market capitalisation of RM5 billion upon listing.
A total of 10,859 applications were received for 175 million units under the public offering, representing an overall subscription rate of 1.59 times.
The non-Bumiputera portion was oversubscribed 1.85 times, with 9,114 applications for 156.76 million units, while the Bumiputera portion received 1,745 applications for 18.24 million units, representing a subscription rate of 0.33 times.
Meanwhile, the restricted offering to entitled shareholders was oversubscribed 1.10 times, with applications for 604.18 million units against 550.61 million units available.
The 55 million units offered to eligible directors, employees and business associates were fully subscribed.
The institutional offering, comprising up to 1.48 billion units, was also fully subscribed, with interest predominantly from long-only investors, including GLICs and insurance companies.
At the IPO price of 91 sen, IOIPG Reit is projected to offer a distribution yield of 6.96 per cent, based on an annualised projected distribution of 6.33 sen per unit for the financial period from Sept 11, 2026, to June 30, 2027.
The final retail price was reduced from the initial 96 sen, with successful retail applicants to receive a refund of five sen for each unit allotted, without interest, within 10 market days from the date of the final ballot applications.
Notices of allotment are expected to be mailed to successful applicants by Nov 24, 2026.

Title: Muhyiddin hopes 'encouraging' reception in Melaka translates into votes
Article:
MELAKA: Bersatu has described the encouraging response from voters in the seven state constituencies it is contesting in the Melaka election as a positive sign ahead of polling day on Saturday.
Its president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin said the party's campaign efforts had made good progress, judging by the encouraging turnout at its programmes in several constituencies since the campaign began.
He cited Pantai Kundor as an example, where a large crowd attended a campaign programme for Bersatu candidate Datin Seri Dr Asmah Ibrahim.
He hoped the support shown by voters throughout the campaign period would translate into votes on Nov 14.
"Based on our observations, the response from nearly half the voters in those areas (seven constituencies) has been very encouraging," he told reporters after attending the Berjalan Untuk Perubahan programme in Pantai Puteri here today.
Also present were Bersatu secretary-general and Melaka election director Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali and Bersatu information chief Datuk Tun Faisal Ismail Aziz.
Muhyiddin said candidates for the seven seats were selected based on specific qualifications, with the party also explaining its objectives and reasons for contesting in the respective constituencies.
On a related matter, Muhyiddin urged voters living outside Melaka to return home to cast their ballots on polling day.
