Title: PKFZ ready to open records, facilitate audits amid cooking oil traceability concerns
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — The Port Klang Free Zone (PKFZ) says it is prepared to provide relevant reports and facilitate regulatory audits amid concerns over the origin, authenticity and traceability of cooking oil products allegedly blended before being re-exported under Malaysian labels.
PKFZ chairman Lim Lip Eng said the free zone would extend its full cooperation to the relevant authorities.
“We will provide our full cooperation and assistance, including making available relevant reports and facilitating any audit requests,” he said in a statement.
Lim said PKFZ operated under the Free Zones Act, while enforcement involving product authenticity and regulatory compliance fell under the jurisdiction of the relevant government agencies.
These include the Malaysian Palm Oil Board (MPOB), SIRIM, the Malaysian Quarantine and Inspection Services Department (MAQIS) and the Construction Industry Development Board (CIDB).
His response follows concerns raised last week by Maritime Network Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Datuk Seri R. Jeyenderan Ramasamy over the alleged blending of imported cooking oil with locally produced supplies before it is exported under Malaysian labels.
Jeyenderan said the alleged practice, which industry players have described as an oil “cocktail”, warranted closer scrutiny by the authorities, particularly over product origin, quality and food safety.
His remarks came after
The Edge
reported on Nov 4, citing industry sources, that imported palm oil was allegedly being blended with local supplies before being re-exported, potentially allowing foreign-origin oil to be marketed as Malaysian palm oil. According to the report, blending ratios of 75:25 or 80:20 were circulating in the market.
Jeyenderan said an examination of cargo manifests and bills of lading had raised concerns over how the oil’s country of origin was declared and how its actual composition was verified after blending.
Jeyenderan, who has more than 30 years of experience in the maritime industry, said independent laboratory tests were needed to establish whether the imported oil and the final blended product met the required quality and food safety standards.
He also questioned whether oil samples were tested before the vessels carrying the cargo left Malaysian waters, claiming the vessels concerned were not equipped with specialised laboratory facilities or qualified chemists to carry out detailed analyses.
Jeyenderan said any possibility of contamination should be investigated through scientific testing rather than assumptions.
“If the oil is contaminated, what could be the impact on public health? Who is responsible for ensuring that the final product is safe for consumption?” he had asked previously.
He said international rules already set clear expectations on origin, testing and traceability.
Under the Codex Alimentarius, the international food standards adopted by the United Nations’ Food and Agriculture Organization and World Health Organization, the General Standard for the Labelling of Prepackaged Foods requires a food’s country of origin to be declared if leaving it out would mislead or deceive consumers.
“Codex only allows the origin to shift when processing changes the nature of the food. Simply mixing imported oil with Malaysian oil does not change its nature, so declaring the blend as wholly Malaysian may mislead buyers,” he was quoted saying.
On testing, he noted that international palm oil trade contracts under FOSFA International, including FOSFA Contract No. 81 issued jointly with the Palm Oil Refiners Association of Malaysia (PORAM), require independent analysis by qualified surveyors.
He also warned that Article 3 of the European Union Deforestation Regulation (EUDR), which will apply to large operators from December 30, 2026, requires palm oil entering the EU to be traceable to the plots of land where it was produced.
He urged the authorities to clarify the procedures governing the import, blending, sampling, quality certification and re-export of cooking oil, including which agencies are responsible for monitoring each stage.
He said proper documentation and independent laboratory testing were essential to ensure that products exported from Malaysia complied with the required standards and that their country of origin was accurately declared.
He added that failing to address the concerns could affect consumer confidence and Malaysia’s reputation as a food exporter.

Title: Najib’s house arrest: Malaysian Bar entitled to challenge Pardons Board decision, says Azalina
Article:
BANGI, Nov 12 — The Malaysian Bar has the right to challenge the Federal Territories Pardons Board’s decision allowing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest.
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said the Bar is entitled to mount such a challenge if it believes it has grounds to question the decision.
“But I have always stressed that when we speak of matters under Article 42, it is considered what is referred to as the prerogative of mercy, which we know is among the powers fully vested in the discretion of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, the power of pardon.
“So it is up to the Malaysian Bar as to what it wants to bring... If the Malaysian Bar feels it has the right to question any issue, that is its right,” she told reporters here today.
She said this after the certificate presentation ceremony for the Professional Mediation Certification Course and Mediator Appointment Certificates, as well as the launch of the Madani Mediation Centre Handbook, Legal Aid Department 2026.
The Attorney-General’s Chambers (AGC) today objected to the Malaysian Bar’s bid to challenge the Federal Territories Pardons Board’s decision allowing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak to serve the remainder of his prison sentence in the SRC International Sdn Bhd case under house arrest.
Senior federal counsel Ahmad Hanir Hambaly@Arwi informed High Court Judge S. Indra Nehru today that the AGC had received the Bar’s application for leave to commence judicial review by email two days earlier and needed time to file written submissions.
Meanwhile, Najib’s lawyer Muhammad Farhan Muhammad Shafee informed the court that his client also intended to file written submissions, as any decision by the court after leave is granted could affect him.
Lawyer Zainur Zakaria, representing the Malaysian Bar, did not object to the requests by the AGC and Najib’s lawyers for time to file their respective written submissions.
Judge Indra Nehru fixed March 17 next year to hear the application and directed both parties to file their respective written submissions by December 14, with replies to be filed on or before December 28.
On November 10, the Bar filed the judicial review application naming the Federal Territories Pardons Board, the Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform), the Director-General of Prisons and Najib as respondents. — Bernama

Title: KTMB: MyKomuter50 pass activation begins Nov 16, offering 30 days of unlimited travel on selected routes from Dec 1
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — The public can start activating the MyKomuter50 Pass on November 16 to enjoy unlimited travel for 30 days on selected KTM Komuter services for RM50, with savings of up to 88 per cent, effective December 1.
In a statement today, Keretapi Tanah Melayu Bhd (KTMB) said the pass, aimed at easing the cost of living, was particularly beneficial to those commuting to work and educational institutions.
For example, users travelling on the Tanjung Malim-KL Sentral route, who would normally spend RM416 on fares over 30 days, would only need to pay RM50 with the pass, saving RM366 or nearly 88 per cent.
“For the Alor Setar-Butterworth route, users can save up to RM234, or about 82 per cent, compared with the estimated regular fare of RM284 over the same period and frequency of travel,” KTMB said.
The pass is open to Malaysian citizens aged seven and above who are not holders of the MyRailLife Pass. Applicants must present their MyKad or MyKid for eligibility verification.
Verification can be done through the KTM Mobile or KITS Style applications by uploading a copy of the identification document, a process that may take up to three working days.
Alternatively, users can obtain immediate verification at ticket kiosks or counters at KTM Komuter stations.
KTMB said activation and purchase facilities would be available at 34 selected stations, comprising 10 KTM Komuter Northern Sector stations, 20 Klang Valley KTM Komuter stations and four Southern Shuttle stations. An additional 11 registration counters would also be provided.
The pass is available at RM50 for each of the three service categories, namely MyKomuter50 Northern Sector, MyKomuter50 Klang Valley and MyKomuter50 Southern Shuttle.
KTMB encouraged users to complete the eligibility verification, activation and purchase processes on the same day.
Further information is available at www.ktmb.com.my or through the KTMB Call Centre at 03-9779 1200. — Bernama

Title: Anwar joins Pakatan campaign trail in Melaka ahead of Saturday’s state polls
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 12 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim joined the coalition’s campaign trail in Melaka today as campaigning intensified ahead of Saturday’s state election.
The prime minister, who is also PKR president, began his campaign activities with a walkabout at shoplots and hawker stalls in Taman Krubong Jaya at about 6pm.
Accompanied by PH’s candidate for the Paya Rumput state seat, Datuk Azman Abidin, Anwar spent around 30 minutes mingling with hawkers, traders and residents, many of whom took the opportunity to greet him and take photographs.
He then proceeded to Kampung Machap Baru before attending the Ngopi Santai programme in Ayer Molek.
Anwar’s evening itinerary included the Melaka Rumah Kita programme at the Hang Tuah Jaya parliamentary service centre in Bukit Baru, followed by Melaka Rumah Kita carnival at Taman Melaka Perdana in Alor Gajah.
In the 16th Melaka polls, PH is fielding the most candidates, contesting 24 of the 28 state seats, followed by Barisan Nasional (23), Parti Bersama Malaysia (16), Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (seven), Perikatan Nasional (five) and Parti Bumiputera Perkasa Malaysia (one). Three independent candidates are also contesting.
The Election Commission has set polling for Saturday, with 687,697 registered voters eligible to cast their ballots.
For the latest news on the state polls, visit
https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/
. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia’s FRIM puts century-old library collection online, opening 77,600 digital files to public
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — More than a century’s worth of knowledge and information on tropical forest biodiversity and science from the Forest Research Institute Malaysia (FRIM) is now accessible worldwide through its digital repository, the FRIM Research Depository (FRED).
FRIM said in a statement today that the FRED portal, fully operational since last year, recorded an average of 2,885 user accesses annually and offered free registration for round-the-clock access to 160,244 metadata records and 77,600 digital files.
The digital resources include scientific articles, books, theses, journals, forest maps and newspaper clippings, benefiting researchers, policymakers, industry players, students and the public.
“This digitalisation initiative marks a transformation from the physical services of the FRIM Library in Kepong, which receives an average of 2,200 visitors annually,” the statement said.
Established before 1918 and having survived both British and Japanese administrations, the specialised library houses nearly 200,000 reference materials covering 82 subjects related to forestry and forest products.
FRIM said historical records and documents preserved in the library were also among the key contributors to FRIM’s recognition as a Unesco World Heritage Site.
“To ensure authoritative and systematically organised scientific references, the library’s collection is managed using the Global Forestry Decimal Classification (GFDC), an international hierarchical classification standard also adopted by the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) and the International Union of Forest Research Organisations (IUFRO),” the statement said.
Besides preserving heritage manuscripts from physical deterioration, the library houses four major special collections, namely the Rattan Collection, Bamboo Collection, Asean Collection and FRIRO (FRIM Research Output) Collection.
According to FRIM, the Rattan Collection was developed in 1988 through the Rattan Information Centre (RIC), with funding from the Canadian International Development Agency (CIDA), to promote rattan species such as Calamus manan as a scientific commodity and support rural economies.
The Bamboo Collection, established in 1993, contains more than 1,200 reference materials on bamboo research and industry, while the Asean Collection comprises research reports, proceedings on traditional forest management and studies on the regional impact of climate change.
Meanwhile, the FRIRO (FRIM Research Output) Collection serves as the official repository of publications, consultancy reports and conference papers produced by FRIM researchers since 1990.
“Since the establishment of the Forestry School in 1927 and academic collaboration with the Faculty of Forestry at Universiti Putra Malaysia (UPM) beginning in 1971, the FRIM Library has remained a cornerstone of human capital development and forestry education in the country.
“In today’s era of information overload, the FRED portal ensures that the public has access to authentic, reliable and rigorously evaluated scientific references,” the statement said.
Members of the public and the research community can explore the country’s wealth of tropical forest science knowledge through the FRED portal at
https://fred.frim.gov.my/Home/Index_v3
. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia selects Turkiye as preferred alternative missile supplier for Navy’s LCS project, says defence minister
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — Turkiye has been selected as the preferred country to supply an alternative to Norway’s Naval Strike Missile (NSM) for the Royal Malaysian Navy’s (RMN) Littoral Combat Ship (LCS) project.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the decision was made after the government evaluated proposals from several countries, including Turkiye, France and Italy, based on price, delivery timelines and upfront costs.
“We have conducted an evaluation and have now reached the stage of determining that Turkiye is the best country from which to obtain an alternative to our missile.
“We will engage with the Turkish side for further negotiations so that we can finalise the matter,” he told reporters after the Defence Ministry’s 2026 Innovation Day celebration at the Mindef Auditorium today.
He said the government had also received assurances on the missile’s compatibility and integration with the ships’ systems, which would be further examined during negotiations with the Turkish company.
Mohamed Khaled said the missile from Turkiye was of the same type as that already ordered for the Royal Malaysian Navy’s (RMN) Littoral Combat Ship (LCS) project, allowing supplies to be obtained earlier, as early as 2028.
He said the surface-to-surface missile had an operational range of 240 kilometres, with comparable explosive power and greater effectiveness than competing missiles.
In terms of cost, he said Malaysia would not have to bear the full cost of procuring new missiles, as part of the expense had already been absorbed under the LCS contract. Instead, the government would likely only need to cover the cost of installing the launchers and integrating the systems.
“If we did not have the LCS, we would have to order new missiles, which could cost RM700 million, RM800 million or RM900 million. Now, we do not need to spend that amount to replace the NSM,” he said.
On the procurement of the NSM from Norway, Mohamed Khaled said the project had stalled because the Norwegian government had not issued the required licence, meaning Malaysia would not receive the missiles despite having made payment for the procurement.
He said the government was now prepared to take legal action through arbitration, but was bound by several stages of dispute resolution stipulated in the contract, after initial negotiations reached a deadlock.
“We are therefore moving to the second stage, which is to establish a Dispute Resolution Committee between the two parties. If that process fails, Malaysia will proceed to arbitration, which can be held in Kuala Lumpur under the NSM procurement contract,” he said.
Meanwhile, Mohamed Khaled said Malaysia was not waiting for the process to be concluded before seeking a replacement for the NSM, to ensure that the country’s defence needs continued to be addressed while the process with Norway was ongoing. — Bernama

Title: Anwar: Malaysia must tap China ties to grow exports and open markets for local products
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — Malaysia should make the most of its strong ties with China to boost exports and expand markets for local products, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, said the Madani Government would continue to strengthen the business environment and help micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) expand their reach in international markets.
“This will ensure that more local businesses benefit from the economic ties between the two countries,” he said in a Facebook post today.
Earlier, Anwar received a courtesy call from the organising committee of the Malaysia-China Entrepreneurs Conference (MCEC) 2026, led by its adviser, Tan Sri Barry Goh Ming Choon, to discuss plans for the 16th edition of the prestigious conference.
Anwar said the government fully supported this year's conference as a strategic platform to strengthen trade, investment and business networks between the corporate communities of both countries.
“I hope MCEC will continue to open up more high-value economic opportunities, including helping local entrepreneurs and Bumiputera companies gain a foothold in the Chinese market, particularly in the halal industry,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Twelve Filipinos, including six children, detained in Labuan immigration crackdown
Article:
LABUAN, Nov 12 — Twelve Filipino nationals, including six children, were detained for suspected immigration offences during an enforcement operation on this duty-free island early today.
Labuan Immigration Department director Mohd Redzuan Nawi said the operation, codenamed Op Sapu, was conducted from 11pm yesterday to 1.30am today, involving 15 officers who inspected 84 individuals at several locations, including a residential settlement.
He said those inspected comprised 51 Malaysians, 31 Filipinos and two Indonesians.
“The 12 Filipinos detained comprised one man, five women, four boys and two girls, all suspected of offences under Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63,” he told Bernama today.
Mohd Redzuan said two witness summonses were also issued to assist investigations.
Those detained are being held at the Labuan Immigration Depot and Labuan district police headquarters for further investigation and action.
Mohd Redzuan said the department would continue enforcing the Immigration Act 1959/63, Passports Act 1966, Immigration Regulations 1963 and Anti-Trafficking in Persons and Anti-Smuggling of Migrants Act 2007 (Atipsom).
He also warned that action would be taken against anyone found employing or harbouring undocumented migrants.
Members of the public with information on illegal immigrants can contact the department at 087-421 296, submit complaints through the Public Complaints Management System (SISPAA) at https://imi.spab.gov.my/eApps/system/index.do, or email pro_labuan@imi.gov.my. — Bernama

Title: Consumers in Malaysia may soon be able to check chicken’s halal status under proposed new rules
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — The Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry (KPDN) is prepared to introduce regulations under the Trade Descriptions Act 2011 to enable consumers to check the sources of slaughterhouses and the halal certification status of chicken sold in the market.
Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali said the move was among efforts to strengthen protection for Muslim consumers following concerns raised by members of parliament over the monitoring and transparency of the halal status of chicken supplies.
He said KPDN also agreed with a proposal by Datuk Idris Ahmad (PN-Bagan Serai) that responsibility for ensuring the integrity of the halal supply chain should not rest solely with the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (Jakim) and state religious authorities, but should also involve KPDN in enforcement and local authorities (PBT) in monitoring business premises.
“Therefore, KPDN will propose better coordination with state religious authorities, local authorities and the Health Ministry to improve the monitoring of slaughterhouses and chicken sales premises,” he said in the Dewan Rakyat today.
He was winding up the debate on the Supply Bill (Budget 2027) and the 2027 Development Expenditure Estimates at the committee stage for the ministry.
On the proposal to restrict eligibility for purchasing packet cooking oil to recipients of the Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) assistance, Armizan said it was a good suggestion, but its implementation would need to be phased in to avoid affecting small traders, including night market vendors.
He said the government first needed to stabilise the implementation of targeted diesel and petrol subsidies before considering more comprehensive reforms to subsidies for other essential goods.
On the Electronic Cooking Oil Price Stabilisation Scheme (eCOSS), Armizan said the system enabled the government to obtain more comprehensive data on the supply, sale and purchase of packet cooking oil, helping it determine quota reductions and better target subsidies based on actual data.
“eCOSS was introduced in May 2023 to monitor the distribution of subsidised packet cooking oil from repackagers to wholesalers and retailers. This was followed by the Mobile eCOSS application, which records consumers’ purchase details through QR code scanning,” he said.
Earlier, during the debate, several MPs raised concerns about enforcement at chicken slaughterhouses whose halal status was in doubt, following a recent raid on a slaughterhouse in Puchong that led to the seizure of 6.5 tonnes of raw chickens and the arrest of 12 foreign workers.
Among them was Idris, who stressed that the issue should not be viewed from a political perspective but treated seriously, as it could undermine consumer confidence in the halal status of food products in the country.
Meanwhile, Mohamad Shafizan Kepli (GPS-Batang Lupar) proposed that the ministry consider issuing Budi Madani petrol and diesel sales permits to selected grocery shops in remote areas, as well as providing MyKad verification terminals to allow eligible residents to access subsidies without compromising efforts to prevent leakages.
The Dewan Rakyat subsequently approved KPDN’s 2027 operating and development expenditure estimates totalling RM2,366,037,400, with a majority vote after 17 MPs took part in the debate. — Bernama

Title: Four foreigners arrested over robbery, assault of cop in Penang; remanded for six days until Nov 17
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM, Nov 12 — Penang police have arrested four Pakistani nationals, including two women, to assist in investigations into a robbery in which a 43-year-old policeman was injured by suspects armed with sharp objects near a petrol station in Permatang Pauh on Tuesday.
Penang Chief Police Officer Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng said the four suspects, aged between 23 and 36, had been remanded for six days until November 17 to facilitate investigations.
“Police are conducting further investigations into the incident. All four suspects were arrested in two raids in Kuala Lumpur yesterday afternoon and early this morning,” he told Bernama when contacted today.
He said the case was being investigated under Section 394 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt while committing robbery.
The policeman was injured after being robbed by four suspects armed with sharp objects near the entrance to a petrol station in Jalan Samagagah, Permatang Pauh, on Tuesday.
Seberang Perai Tengah District Police Chief ACP Nik Aminuddin Raja Abdullah was previously reported as saying that the incident, which occurred at about 11.30am, was believed to involve foreign suspects from a Central Asian country, including two women.
He said the suspects allegedly acted aggressively and used a sharp metal object to injure the victim before fleeing with his personal belongings, resulting in estimated losses of RM10,000.
The group’s modus operandi was to approach members of the public at petrol stations seeking monetary donations before carrying out robberies. — Bernama

Title: Man hanging cat from four-wheel-drive vehicle in Kluang sparks online outrage
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Nov 12 — A video and an image showing a man hanging a cat by its neck from the window of a four-wheel-drive vehicle in Kluang, Johor, have sparked outrage on social media.
Several social media posts claimed the incident took place at Batu Dua, Jalan Mersing, in Kluang.
The incident was reportedly captured on video by someone in a nearby car before the footage was shared online.
The footage and image have drawn widespread condemnation, with social media users expressing anger and sadness over the apparent cruelty towards the animal.
Some also questioned why no one had intervened to confront the driver or rescue the cat.
It remains unclear whether the cat survived or what prompted the man’s actions.
Kluang police chief Assistant Commissioner Bahrin Mohd Noh said police had not received any reports regarding the alleged incident.
However, he said police would conduct an investigation and attempt to identify the individual involved.
The incident comes amid several recent reports of cruelty involving cats, including a case involving the alleged sexual abuse of a cat by a man in Pasir Puteh, Kelantan, last month.
This was followed by a viral video purportedly showing a child killing newborn kittens at the Seri Nilam apartment complex in Ampang, Selangor.

Title: Malaysia approves 143 posts for new Public Defender’s Office, says Azalina
Article:
BANGI, Nov 12 — A total of 143 positions have been approved for the establishment of the Public Defender’s Office, with appointments to be made as soon as possible to strengthen access to legal aid services in the country.
The office would be headed by an officer at the JUSA C level, with approval for the establishment of the posts already obtained from the Finance Ministry, said Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.
“This marks a new chapter for the Legal Aid Department (JBG). As we discussed during the debate on amendments to the Legal Aid and Public Defence Act 2025, we looked at the roles the government should play alongside the National Legal Aid Foundation (YBGK), as a substantial amount of government funding goes directly to YBGK.
“Now, we will establish the Public Defender’s Office to work alongside YBGK,” she told reporters after the presentation of certificates for the Professional Mediation Certification Course and appointments of mediators, as well as the launch of the Legal Aid Department’s Madani Mediation Centre Handbook 2026, here today.
Azalina said the Public Defender’s Office was part of the government’s efforts to modernise the legal aid system, moving beyond the traditional approach to provide services that better meet the needs of the public.
She said the amendments to the Legal Aid and Public Defence Act 2025, which were passed by Parliament in August last year, were expected to come into force in the first quarter of 2027.
“What is most important to me is that the public defender works closely with the existing YBGK unit, while continuing to cooperate with the Bar Council and State Bar Committees,” she said.
Meanwhile, Azalina said the government hoped to make mediation part of everyday practice among Malaysians through the establishment of the Madani Mediation Centre (PMM).
She said the initiative would complement the existing legal aid services provided by JBG under the Legal Aid Act by offering another avenue for alternative dispute resolution.
“With mediation, people can come to JBG to seek an alternative dispute resolution platform through the mediation services offered under PMM.
“This is a more people-centric approach as it gives parties in a dispute the opportunity to resolve their differences through mediation,” she said.
At the event, 210 participants completed six series of the Professional Mediation Certification Course organised by JBG in collaboration with Universiti Sains Islam Malaysia and the National Legal Training Institute.
The programme was funded through an allocation of RM680,000 under the 2026 Budget Initiative to strengthen mediation expertise in the public sector.
Azalina also launched the Madani Mediation Centre Handbook, developed by JBG as a key reference to ensure that case-handling procedures, professional ethics and mediation service standards are implemented systematically and consistently nationwide. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia’s fiscal reforms set to lower federal debt ratio to 63.7pc by 2027, says Treasury sec-gen
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — The Madani government is committed to gradually reducing the fiscal deficit from 5.5 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 2022 to 3.3 per cent in 2027.
Treasury secretary-general Tan Sri Johan Mahmood Merican said the reduction in the fiscal deficit reflects the government’s commitment to strengthen the country’s financial position, thereby helping to lower the ratio of the federal government’s debt to GDP.
He said the ratio of the federal government’s debt to GDP, which was 65.2 per cent at the end of 2025, was projected to decrease to 64 per cent at the end of this year and further to 63.7 per cent in 2027.
“This is part of the government’s efforts to carry out fiscal reforms to ensure that the level of debt is at the appropriate level,” he told reporters at Deloitte’s 52nd TaxMax conference here today.
He said the fiscal expansion policy in Budget 2027 is key to supporting economic growth, keeping the unemployment rate low, and increasing people’s income to help households deal with the cost-of-living challenge.
Commenting on the proposed re-implementation of the Goods and Services Tax (GST), he said the move may not be appropriate at this time, given economic uncertainty and the government’s priority to increase people’s income amid the cost-of-living challenge.
He said the government still prioritises efforts to increase people’s income, including through a minimum wage increase.
Johan said the proposal to replace the Sales and Service Tax (SST) with GST at an equivalent rate would not necessarily increase government revenue, but rather potentially shift part of the tax burden from the business sector, including exporters, to consumers.
“The Prime Minister has commented on the issue of GST and SST several times. Although GST may have its advantages, it may not be the right time at this juncture.
“There may also be some misunderstandings or misinterpretations, which are not accurate, with some parties suggesting to implement GST to increase revenue.
He said that those who propose introducing GST to increase the country’s revenue may need a higher GST rate, and that is not something the government wants at this time.
To date, Johan said SST collections stand at 3.2 per cent of GDP, the same ratio as GST collections in 2017. — Bernama

Title: Anwar chairs special meeting as Selangor steps up efforts to tackle recurring floods
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 12 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today chaired a special meeting on Selangor flood disaster coordination at Parliament House to streamline efforts to address recurring floods in the state.
Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the meeting focused on four key actions, including strengthening early warning systems with the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) and improving disaster management coordination by the Selangor State Disaster Management Committee.
The other two key actions involve resolving flash floods through the Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID) and studying Kuala Lumpur City Hall’s (DBKL) flood management best practices.
“Special attention is being given to flood-prone areas, particularly in the Petaling and Kuala Selangor districts, which recorded 1,180 evacuees at seven temporary relief centres as of November 12, 2026.
“I want every one of these actions implemented immediately, including accelerating flood mitigation efforts and upgrading drainage systems to reduce the risk of recurring floods,” he said in a social media post.
Amirudin said the meeting was also attended by state government representatives, state executive councillors, state assemblymen, district officers, and relevant agencies, including the National Disaster Management Agency (NADMA), DID, the Public Works Department (JKR), and the Selangor Implementation Coordination Unit (ICU).
Meanwhile, he said the welfare of flood victims remains a priority, including channelling the Selangor People’s Flood Disaster Special Aid totalling RM3,000 to each eligible head of household, subject to set conditions.
“I understand the people’s anxiety, especially those who repeatedly face floods. Therefore, I want every plan translated into immediate, tangible action, not just discussions,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Kelantan reassigns Culture and Heritage portfolio to Zamakshari Muhamad after Kamaruddin Mohd Noor dropped from exco
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Nov 12 — Kelantan Youth, Sports, NGOs and Community Unity Committee chairman Zamakshari Muhamad has been entrusted with overseeing the state’s Culture and Heritage portfolio.
He said the responsibility was not merely an addition to his existing duties, but a significant responsibility to ensure that the state’s cultural heritage, arts, customs and traditions continued to be preserved and passed down to future generations.
He said Kelantan had a distinct cultural identity, rich in historical values, traditions, arts and local wisdom, which formed part of the identity of its people.
“I will focus on efforts to preserve and document historical heritage and customs, as well as strengthen local arts and culture in line with Islamic principles and the values of Kelantan society.
“The involvement of the younger generation as heirs, practitioners and future custodians of culture and heritage should also be encouraged. Strategic cooperation with government agencies, cultural institutions, artists, non-governmental organisations (NGOs) and local communities will also be expanded,” he said in a statement today.
Yesterday, the media reported that Ayer Lanas assemblyman Datuk Kamaruddin Mohd Noor would not have his appointment as a Kelantan State Executive Council (Exco) member renewed, effective November 9. — Bernama

Title: Sarawak targets year-end pilot launch for ART service on Rembus-Northbank route, says Abang Johari
Article:
KUCHING, Nov 12 — Pilot operations of the Autonomous Rapid Transit (ART) service along the initial Rembus-Northbank route are targeted to begin by the end of this year, said Caretaker Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg.
He said the service would further integrate Samarahan into the Kuching Urban Transportation System (KUTS), which uses ART technology as a key component of Sarawak’s modern public transport network.
“With the ART depot located in Rembus, Samarahan has become part of the main network of the modern public transportation system being developed by the Sarawak government,” he said.
His speech at the Kota Samarahan Municipal Council’s (MPKS) 10th Anniversary Dinner on Wednesday was read out by Caretaker Tourism, Creative Industry and Performing Arts Minister and Asajaya incumbent Dato Sri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah.
Abang Johari said commercial ART services would be introduced in stages following the pilot phase.
“Once operational, the system is expected to improve connectivity between Samarahan and Kuching, provide better transportation options and reduce reliance on private vehicles,” he said.
He said Samarahan’s future connectivity would also be influenced by the proposed development of a new Kuching International Airport at Tanjung Embang, Asajaya.
The proposed airport, he said, could create opportunities in the aviation, logistics, trade, tourism and investment sectors, while spurring the development of road networks, supporting infrastructure and economic activities in surrounding areas.
“Therefore, I want MPKS, together with the relevant agencies, to take into account land-use planning, infrastructure and public amenity requirements at an early stage so that the anticipated growth can be managed in an orderly manner,” he said.
Abang Johari said Samarahan, with a population approaching 200,000, would face growing demands for public amenities, transportation, infrastructure, cleanliness and a comfortable living environment as development progressed.
He said MPKS therefore had an increasingly important responsibility to ensure efficient municipal services kept pace with the area’s growth.
Also present were Caretaker Deputy Infrastructure and Port Development Minister Datuk Aidel Lariwoo and MPKS chairman Abang Ismawi Abang Ali. — The Borneo Post

Title: Sarawak deputy premier says NCR land surveys will only proceed with owners’ consent
Article:
SIBU, Nov 12 — Native Customary Rights (NCR) land ownership in Sarawak continues to be protected through land surveys conducted only upon the application and consent of stakeholders to prevent boundary disputes, encroachment and the loss of rights to ancestral land.
Sarawak Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Awang Tengah Ali Hasan said every survey application must undergo scrutiny and verification of ownership evidence by the Sarawak Land and Survey Department to ensure the claims are legally valid.
He stressed that the state government would not conduct land surveys arbitrarily without first engaging with and obtaining the consent of landowners or claimants.
“We have stipulated that surveys must be carried out upon application. Before any survey work begins, we hold engagement sessions and discussions with stakeholders.
“We want to avoid misunderstandings or allegations that the government is attempting to seize people’s land,” he said at the presentation ceremony for Native Communal Reserve gazette notifications, land titles and land compensation cheques for Sibu Division here today.
Awang Tengah said NCR land surveys would not be carried out on land subject to unresolved ownership disputes or pending court cases until the matters had been settled.
He said that since the introduction of the new NCR land survey initiative in 2010 until October 31 this year, a total of 1,248,659 hectares had undergone perimeter surveys, of which 979,434 hectares had been gazetted as Native Communal Reserves.
During the same period, 112,717 individual lots covering 135,332 hectares had been surveyed, while land titles had been issued for 40,796 lots covering 60,727 hectares.
At the ceremony, 167 land titles were presented to 158 recipients, while five areas covering 21,942.13 hectares in Sibu and Kanowit were gazetted as Native Communal Reserves.
The state government also distributed RM12.69 million in land compensation to 165 recipients affected by five development projects in Sibu Division. — Bernama

Title: Penang to consult stakeholders on raising Muslim marriage age to 18
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 12 — The Penang government will hold engagement sessions to explore the possibility of raising the minimum age for Muslims to marry to 18, following similar moves by Selangor and Kedah.
Deputy Chief Minister I Datuk Mohamad Abdul Hamid, who is also Penang Islamic Religious Council (MAINPP) president, said the sessions would be held to gather views and assess whether the proposed change could be implemented in the state.
“So far, no discussions have been held on the proposal. We may first organise engagement sessions to explore whether it can be implemented in Penang.
“The sessions will also involve the Women, Family and Community Development Ministry before any decision is made or further developments are announced,” he told reporters here today.
Mohamad was speaking after witnessing the signing of a cooperation agreement between the Penang Islamic Foundation (YIPP) and Idrissi International School. Also present were YIPP chief executive Dr Mohamad Sofee Razak and Idrissi founder Zaliza Alias.
Mohamad said the minimum age for Muslims to marry in Penang remained 16.
He said the state government would gather information and views from the relevant parties through the engagement sessions before considering its next course of action.
He was responding to reports that only Selangor and Kedah had amended their respective laws to raise the minimum marriage age for Muslims to 18, while other states were still subject to their own deliberations and legislative processes.
Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri was previously reported as saying that the government, through her ministry, would continue efforts to gradually standardise the minimum marriage age at 18 nationwide in close cooperation with state governments.
She said the effort would require engagement with state religious authorities, relevant agencies and stakeholders, as Islamic family law falls under the jurisdiction of state governments. — Bernama

Title: Sabah Fire Dept urges public to avoid rivers, waterfalls during monsoon
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Nov 12 — The public is reminded to adhere to safety advice and take necessary precautions when dealing with floods, as well as to postpone all water-based recreational activities during the current North-east Monsoon (MTL) season.
Sabah Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) director Mohd Pisar Aziz said residents must immediately move to relief centres when instructed by the authorities or if rising floodwaters threaten their homes.
He cautioned the public against wading through flooded areas, whether on foot or by vehicle, as the depth of the water and strength of the currents could sweep anyone away.
“Parents are also reminded to monitor their children’s movements and prohibit them from playing in floodwaters to avoid the risk of drowning or other dangers,” he told Bernama.
He said that to avoid the risk of electric shocks, residents should switch off the main power supply before leaving their homes, provided it was safe to do so, and avoid touching electrical appliances in wet areas.
He also called on the public to stay clear of any severed or fallen electrical cables and to immediately report the matter to the authorities or Sabah Electricity Sdn Bhd.
Mohd Pisar also advised the public to postpone all water-based recreational activities, including bathing, swimming, picnicking and camping near rivers, rapids, waterfalls and irrigation canals throughout the Northeast Monsoon season.
He said this was crucial due to the unpredictable weather conditions and persistent heavy rain in upstream catchment areas, which could cause water levels to rise abruptly and trigger sudden water surges that could claim lives within seconds.
“Water surges can happen in the blink of an eye following heavy rain in catchment areas, and the public should not wait until the water flowt becomes strong before taking action,” he added.
Mohd Pisar also reminded the public to remain vigilant always and stay updated on weather forecasts, comply with instructions from the authorities and heed safety warning signs placed at popular recreational spots.
He urged the public to immediately contact the emergency hotline at 999 in the event of an emergency or upon noticing early signs of a water surge to enable rescue operations to be launched without delay.
The public is also reminded to raise fire safety awareness at home by instilling safety-conscious practices from an early age.
He advised parents to keep an eye on their children to prevent them from playing with electrical switches or appliances unsupervised, while ensuring their hands are always dry and to avoid overloading electrical sockets.
“If a fire breaks out or smoke is detected in a home, occupants should leave immediately through a safe exit in a calm manner and assist family members without re-entering the premises,” he added.
He reminded the public not to attempt to put out a fire if the situation posed a threat to their lives, but instead leave the task to the fire and rescue personnel.
He stressed that fire prevention was a collective responsibility shared by all levels of society, complementing the department’s role as the nation’s main rescue agency. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia tightens screening of foreign students to protect higher education standards
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — The admission of international students to higher education institutions (HEIs) in the country continues to be subject to a stringent screening process to ensure that only qualified candidates are accepted, thereby preventing them from becoming a burden to the nation.
Higher Education director-general Datuk Prof Dr Azlinda Azman said particular emphasis was placed on cumulative grade point average (CGPA) and English language proficiency as key eligibility requirements to safeguard the quality of the country’s higher education.
“We want to ensure that quality standards remain at the highest level and not admit students indiscriminately, only for them to eventually create problems or become a burden to the country,” she told Bernama after officiating the Education Summit Kuala Lumpur here today.
Commenting on language requirements, Azlinda said all foreign students, including postgraduate students, were required to undergo a one-semester Bahasa Melayu course upon enrolment at local universities, particularly public universities (UA).
She said the measure would enable them to communicate in the national language in their daily affairs while fostering an understanding of the cultural diversity of the local community.
“Interestingly, most of these international students achieve excellent results in the subject because Bahasa Melayu is actually easy to learn,” she said.
Meanwhile, she said Education Malaysia Global Services (EMGS) and the NAMA Foundation were actively mobilising efforts to secure funding contributors to offer full and partial scholarship schemes for international students.
Azlinda said the funding initiative could help cover students’ living expenses while driving the target of attracting 500,000 international students by 2035 under the Malaysia Higher Education Blueprint (RPTM) 2026-2035, compared with approximately 170,000 currently.
She said student placements were also aligned with universities’ areas of specialisation, such as marine science at Universiti Malaysia Terengganu (UMT) and artificial intelligence (AI) at Universiti Sains Malaysia (USM) and Asia Pacific University (APU).
Meanwhile, Education Malaysia Global Services (EMGS) Chief Executive Officer Novie Tajuddin said Malaysia had made history as the first country in the world to establish a 24-hour International Student Arrival Centre (ISAC) at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) to facilitate the entry of foreign students.
“This is a unique initiative that has never been implemented by any other country and serves as an added value in terms of hospitality, distinguishing Malaysia from other study destinations,” he said.
He said the facility, officially introduced early this year, operated on a three-shift basis with the support of four dedicated immigration lanes.
In addition, Novie said the focus on student welfare had enabled Malaysia to rise from outside the world’s top 20 to the group of 14 leading countries (“Big 14”), while also ranking among the world’s top three in terms of annual and five-year growth rates in international student enrolment.
In 2025, EMGS received more than 95,000 international student applications, an increase of approximately 17 per cent compared with 2024, bringing the number of foreign students in the country to more than 167,000 from over 180 countries.
At today’s conference, six universities signed memoranda of agreement (MoAs) with EMGS and the NAMA Foundation to support funding and welfare for foreign students. — Bernama

Title: Malaysian Indian youths see education system as source of discrimination, Iman Research report finds
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — Indian youths in Malaysia see the national education system as a significant source of discrimination rather than a pathway to social mobility, according to a report released today by Iman Research.
The study, titled
The Kita Orang Sini Juga – Indian Youth Report
, found that students experienced social alienation and institutional bias throughout their schooling, sometimes at the hands of those responsible for guiding their development.
The report cited a 2021 survey by youth movement Sekolah Semua, which found that nine in 10 Indian students felt they had experienced discrimination because of their ethnicity; based on 2,441 responses nationwide, 73 per cent said they faced discrimination from their peers, while 74 per cent reported similar experiences involving teachers.
Discrimination in schools
Drawing on interviews with 111 Indian youths nationwide, Iman Research documented instances in which educators, who were expected to act as mentors, allegedly reinforced negative stereotypes and made students feel unwelcome.
One respondent described being denied leadership opportunities at a semi-urban school and repeatedly made to feel inadequate by teachers.
“The teachers would directly tell me, you can come from this interview, but I’ll tell you now itself, I will not give you this position... It really made me feel so inferior in that school.
I’m really such a nobody here. I cannot do anything. I cannot grow,” the report quoted the youth as saying.
Another respondent recalled an incident in which a Bahasa Melayu teacher allegedly used derogatory language to distinguish between Indian students based on their perceived behaviour.
“[The] BM teacher came into my class one day, straight up used ‘
keling
’. He said, ‘
you budak India ke budak keling
?’ Yeah, then he pointed at me and said ‘
kalau you India you baik, kalau keling macam
-’ then he pointed at other [Indian] students,” the youth recalled.
The report said such experiences could leave students feeling isolated and pressured to navigate “respectability politics”, whereby they felt compelled to behave exceptionally well to avoid negative generalisations about their community.
Structural barriers
Beyond individual experiences in classrooms, the report identified the matriculation quota system as a structural obstacle for Indian youths seeking access to higher education, with limited places and inadequate educational resources contributing to frustration among respondents from different states.
It also highlighted concerns over access to mother-tongue education and challenged the assumption that national schools automatically foster unity, noting that Indian students continued to encounter segregation and “ingroup-outgroup” dynamics, which could be learned from their surroundings, including parents and teachers, from as early as kindergarten.
The report further found that socio-economic status did not necessarily shield Indian students from discrimination, citing the experience of a middle-class student who was initially blamed by teachers after being physically attacked by a group of peers.
“It was five or six versus one. It was a physical fight. I got scolded once the fight ended and blamed, and when the teachers found out they didn’t realise at that point that my mum was a teacher, but when they found out then they were like, I remember the teacher apologised for scolding me,” the report quoted the youth as saying.
The report concluded that failing to protect students from discriminatory behaviour risks normalising racism and weakening young people’s confidence in institutional fairness, ultimately shaping how they view their political influence and place in Malaysian society.

Title: Penang CM: Loke’s resignation ‘painful’, but shows his principles
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 12 — DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke Siew Fook’s resignation as transport minister was a “painful” decision but reflected his willingness to take responsibility based on principles, said Penang Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman Chow Kon Yeow.
Chow said Loke’s decision was not an easy one, especially given the public attention surrounding a court decision involving former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak.
“I view Anthony Loke’s resignation as a decision that pains us. This is because the reason for his resignation is public knowledge, namely the issue that is still being discussed and has yet to be resolved,” he said after attending PBA Holdings Bhd’s extraordinary general meeting here today.
He was commenting on Loke’s resignation as transport minister with immediate effect on November 10.
Chow, who is also a DAP central committee member, said the decision showed that Loke was not putting his own interests first but was willing to take responsibility to convey an important message to the country.
He said the move also signalled that the country’s interests must be protected to ensure a positive direction for development and uphold the dignity of the people.
“So, the resignation was not an easy choice to make, but after taking those considerations into account, Loke was willing to shoulder the responsibility,” he said.
Asked whether Loke’s expertise could be used to assist Penang DAP or other state governments, Chow said the matter would have to be discussed with those who possessed the relevant expertise.
He said the party was always open to considering various measures to address the political issues and challenges it faced.
Chow said Loke’s resignation had also received the backing of DAP’s central executive committee (CEC), and that any subsequent steps would likewise be discussed by the party leadership.
“I believe that whatever the next steps are, they will be discussed and considered by the CEC so that a wise and sustainable decision can be made,” he said.

Title: Flood evacuee numbers in Selangor, Perak fall from 1,484 to 1,445 as of 4pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — The number of flood evacuees sheltering at temporary relief centres in Selangor and Perak fell slightly this afternoon to 1,445 people from 405 families, down from 1,484 people from 420 families this morning.
In Selangor, the number of victims housed at relief centres in Kuala Selangor dropped to 1,144 as of 4pm, compared with 1,180 this morning.
According to the Social Welfare Department’s (JKM) InfoBencana portal, SK Dato’ Maharaja Lela housed 391 evacuees, followed by Sekolah Rendah Agama Bukit Kuching (283), SK Parit Mahang (248), Sekolah Agama Batu 8 Ijok (71), and SK Jaya Setia (12).
In addition, 89 victims were sheltered at Kafa Integrasi Hidayah and 50 at Dewan Komuniti Penyayang Tanjung Siam.
In Perak, the number of flood evacuees in the Hilir Perak district dipped slightly to 301 this afternoon, down from 304 in the morning.
The State Disaster Management Committee (JPBN) secretariat said 269 evacuees were placed at the Dewan Rumah Rehat Majlis Perbandaran Teluk Intan (MPTI) relief centre and 32 at Dewan MPTI Langkap.
Meanwhile, the Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID) reported that Sungai Kurau at Kolam Air Bukit Merah recorded a warning level of 9.10 metres (m), while Sungai Kampar at Kampung Baru Kuala Dipang (RHN) was at the alert level with a reading of 22.11m. — Bernama

Title: Deep-rooted discrimination leaves Malaysian Indian youths feeling alienated and marginalised, report finds
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — Indian youths in Malaysia are feeling increasingly marginalised, facing systemic discrimination in education, employment, and housing that leaves many feeling politically alienated, according to a new report by think tank Iman Research.
The report, titled
Kami Orang Sini Juga — Indian Youth Report
, launched today, highlights that this demographic is an “under-mobilised constituency” whose concerns have long been overlooked by policymakers and the political establishment.
Based on in-depth interviews with 111 Indian youths nationwide, the study paints a stark picture of the hurdles these young Malaysians face from an early age, ranging from racial hostility in schools to precariousness in the housing and labour markets.
Iman Research researcher Shaleen Surendra highlighted that the findings serve as a critical wake-up call for those in power to address the growing disillusionment within the community.
“Indian youths are an under-mobilised constituency whose concerns have been ignored for too long. Through in-depth interviews, they described the discrimination faced, experiences of precarity towards their belonging, and being politically sidelined,” Shaleen said while presenting the findings.
“The report unpacks the repercussions of leaving these issues unaddressed, namely political alienation and distrust, which will shape the next election and the political landscape of the country,” she added.
From school to workforce
The research details a cycle of systemic failure.
Many Indian youths reported experiencing verbal and, in rarer cases, physical abuse from peers and teachers as early as their schooling years.
While Tamil primary schools were noted to offer a “temporary safety” net, they do not resolve the institutional structures that alienate these students.
The struggle continues into adulthood.
The report identifies that the matriculation system disproportionately affects youths from low-socioeconomic backgrounds, hindering their access to further education.
In the job and rental markets, these youths face inconsistent standards that often lead to outright rejection, forcing many to rely on informal networks that may not always be available to those from lower-income brackets.
Political tokenism and gang recruitment
The report also touches on the political landscape, noting that Indian youth votes are currently “up for grabs.”
However, the study warns that these voters are becoming increasingly savvy to “tokenistic representation.”
Participants expressed deep frustration with agencies such as the Malaysian Indian Transformation Unit (Mitra), which they perceive as lacking impact and reach.
The researchers warned that this disappointment should not be mistaken for apathy; rather, it is a sign that youths are demanding leaders—regardless of ethnicity—who will champion their rights through concrete action.
The consequences of this systemic exclusion remain significant.
The study highlighted that, without proper support systems, at-risk youths, particularly young Indian boys, are increasingly vulnerable to gang recruitment, which offers them a “false sense of safety and belonging.”
A call for structural reform
To bridge the gap between Indian youths and the rest of society, the report calls for comprehensive policy changes, including:
Educational reform:
Shifting the matriculation quota system to a needs-based model and implementing sensitivity training for educators.
Legal protections:
Introducing anti-discrimination legislation to govern hiring processes and rental standards.
Political inclusion:
Establishing town halls and youth councils to bring young people directly into policy discussions and budgeting processes.
Civic engagement:
Increasing transparency in government funding and promoting civic education programmes to mobilise youths beyond traditional party networks.

Title: Sarawak polls: Youths aged 18 to 39 account for nearly one million voters in the state
Article:
KUCHING, Nov 12 — Youths aged 18 to 39 make up nearly half of the 2,058,781 registered voters in Sarawak.
According to the electoral roll as of October 25, Sarawakians aged 30 to 39 made up over one fifth of the total voters, while the 21 to 29 age group had the second largest number of voters.
Sin Chew Daily
reported that voters aged 30 to 39 totalled 441,884, while 405,499 voters were aged between 21 and 29.
The youngest group of voters, aged 18 to 20, totalled 126,712, bringing the total figure for youth voters in Sarawak to 974,095.
“These figures indicate that youth voters play a significant role in determining the outcome of the 13th Sarawak state election,” said the report.
Based on the electoral roll, voters aged from 40 to 49 totalled 353,006, followed by 306,777 voters from the 50 to 59 age group.
In the senior categories, a total of 239,281 voters are aged from 60 to 69, followed by the 70 to 79 age group with 132,303 voters, 80 to 89 age group (40,173 voters), and aged 90 and above group (13,146 voters).
According to the report, Padungan has a higher percentage of senior voters, while Stakan’s voters are relatively younger.
In Padungan, the number of voters aged from 60 to 69 stood at 5,636, followed by the 70 to 79 age group (4,738 voters), 80 to 89 age group (1,873 voters), and 90 and above group (473 voters).
In contrast, Stakan has 3,443 voters aged from 18 to 20, followed by the 21 to 29 age group with 10,554 voters, and 30 to 39 age group (9,119 voters).
Notably, Senadin, which has the highest number of voters at 75,641, also has a higher number of youth constituents.
In Senadin, 6,119 voters are aged from 18 to 20, followed by the 21 to 29 age group with 18,948 voters, and the 30 to 39 age group with 18,531 voters.
“Based on the latest data, there are significant differences in the age structure of the electorate.
“While some constituencies have a higher number of youth voters, other seats recorded more senior and aged voters,” the report added.
On Dec 15, 2021, a non-partisan Malaysian youth movement achieved a milestone in the nation’s political history when amendments to Article 119(1) of the Federal Constitution, which lowered the minimum voting age in Malaysia from 21 to 18, and Automatic Voter Registration (AVR) came into effect.
The 13th Sarawak state election will see these young voters able to exercise their democratic right for the first time. — The Borneo Post

Title: Altantuya case: Mongolia urges Malaysia to seek Sirul’s return with guarantee against execution
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — Mongolia has formally asked Malaysia to intensify talks with Australia for the lawful return of convicted former police officer Sirul Azhar Umar, with effective assurances against the death penalty, as part of a diplomatic push over Altantuya Shaariibuu’s murder.
In a statement today, Mongolia’s special envoy Zandanshatar Gombojav said his government also wanted lawful ways identified for Sirul, currently in Australia, to testify in the civil proceedings.
“Mongolia and Malaysia are friends, and it is because we value this friendship that we raise this matter openly and with respect,” he said.
Mongolia’s Foreign Ministry has delivered an official démarche to Malaysia’s ambassadors in Bangkok and Beijing through its accredited diplomatic missions, while Zandanshatar is in Kuala Lumpur today to convey its positions directly.
The requests follow Mongolia’s expression of profound regret over the Court of Appeal’s January 20, 2026 ruling reversing the Malaysian government’s civil liability for the killing, although it reaffirmed respect for Malaysia’s judicial independence.
Mongolia asked that the legal challenge brought by Altantuya’s father, Dr Shaariibuu Setev, against the ruling and related claims be considered fairly, transparently and strictly on the facts, free from political or external interference.
It also sought prompt examination of any newly discovered or previously unexamined evidence, updates to the family’s legal counsel and an official written status update on the proceedings and matters raised.
On Sirul’s return, Mongolia emphasised that it did not seek anyone’s execution and that any arrangement must include effective assurances against the death penalty.
“A fair and final resolution of this case matters greatly to the trust between our two countries,” Zandanshatar said.
The envoy also launched a global public petition, “Dignity for Altantuya”, addressed to Malaysia and Australia in support of lawful accountability and clear information for the family.
Altantuya was shot dead and her body blown up with explosives in Selangor in October 2006.
The Federal Court reinstated the murder convictions and death sentences of Sirul and fellow former police officer Azilah Hadri in January 2015, after Sirul had fled to Australia in 2014 while on bail.
In the separate civil proceedings, the Shah Alam High Court in December 2022 ordered the two men, former political analyst Abdul Razak Baginda and the Malaysian government to jointly pay Altantuya’s family RM5 million in damages, prompting appeals by the government and Abdul Razak.

Title: Seven scam syndicates targeting victims overseas busted in Sarawak, 28 foreigners among 42 held
Article:
KUCHING, Nov 12 — Police have dismantled seven online scam syndicates operating in Sarawak and arrested 42 individuals, including 28 foreign nationals, during a series of raids under Op Magpie 01/2026.
Sarawak police commissioner Saifullizan Ishak said the operation, coordinated by the Bukit Aman Commercial Crime Investigation Department’s Operations Intelligence Division, was carried out simultaneously across Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah, and Sarawak to combat organised scam call centre activities.
Between October 19 and 31, seven separate raids were conducted in Bintulu, Kuching, Padawan, Miri, and Sibu, targeting syndicates operating out of residential properties — specifically two bungalows, three terraced houses, and two apartment units.
Of the 42 suspects detained, 36 were men and six were women, aged between 19 and 61.
“Among them, 14 were Malaysians, while the remaining 28 were foreign nationals comprising 18 Chinese citizens, eight Indonesians, one Taiwanese national, and one Myanmar national,” he told a press conference here.
He added that the foreign suspects had entered Malaysia as tourists.
To date, 33 individuals have been charged in court, while three others have been made prosecution witnesses.
Of those charged, 17 pleaded guilty and were fined between RM500 and RM4,000 each.
Saifullizan said the syndicates targeted victims in Japan, China, Indonesia, Australia, and Austria through fraudulent investment schemes, cryptocurrency scams, fake online gambling platforms, and love or job scams.
“If you look at the victims of these scams, none were locals; all of them were foreign nationals,” he said.
Investigations revealed the syndicates had been operating for varying durations — the longest-running outfit had been active for about 11 months, while the newest was detected after just 10 days.
During the raids, police seized assets worth an estimated RM230,000, including 33 laptops, four desktop computer sets, seven mobile phones, five Unifi routers, a Starlink satellite internet kit, and a four-wheel-drive vehicle.
Saifullizan noted that scam syndicates have shifted away from conventional telephone lines, relying instead on internet-based calls and satellite systems like Starlink to evade detection.
The cases are being investigated under Sections 420 and 120B of the Penal Code for cheating and criminal conspiracy.
He acknowledged that investigating such syndicates could be challenging as their victims were based overseas, making it difficult for police to obtain evidence directly from them.
Nevertheless, he stressed that police would continue efforts to identify the masterminds, financial networks, and individuals involved in facilitating these operations.
Saifullizan also pointed out that taking legal action against landlords whose properties are misused by syndicates remains challenging, as proving complicity is difficult.
”Based on the statements we have recorded so far, the property owners were genuinely unaware of what was happening,” he said, adding that some landlords focus solely on rental income without vetting their tenants.
As such, he urged property owners to exercise greater caution when renting out their premises, including verifying the identities of tenants and the intended use of their properties.
He further identified abandoned factories, newly developed housing areas, sparsely occupied apartments, and relatively quiet commercial centres as locations commonly targeted by scam syndicates.
Saifullizan called on members of the public to be alert to unusual activities at such premises, particularly frequent movements of people in areas that would otherwise see little activity.
“Therefore, if members of the public notice any unusual activity in these areas, it could indicate the existence of a scam call centre.
“Even if you are unsure, you should still provide us with the information,” he said.
Members of the public with information on suspected online scam operations can contact the Sarawak Commercial Crime Investigation Department on 011-62890089. — The Borneo Post

Title: Saifuddin to suggest declassifying Pardons Board meeting minutes to Cabinet
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail told Parliament today that he would try to put forward proposals to declassify the Federal Territories Pardons Board meeting minutes involving Datuk Seri Mohd Najib Razak at tomorrow's Cabinet meeting.
Saifuddin earlier took on questions about the conditions around Najib's house arrest, which began on Tuesday after the former prime minister secured a fresh High Court order allowing his transfer from Kajang Prison to his residence on Jalan Langgak Duta here.
Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman (MUDA-Muar) had asked if the government plans to make the minutes public amid some backlash and accusations that it supported Najib's conditional pardon, suggesting that "it's not entirely fair the administration is shouldering all the moral burden".
"Muar asked whether it is possible to bring this idea to the Cabinet, for us to declassify not the report in the minutes (but) the minutes of the Pardons Board meeting itself so that it provides fairness or a more accurate perspective on the process through which the Pardons Board operates," Saifuddin said.
"I think that falls within the jurisdiction and responsibility of the Attorney General, but I have no objections," he added.
"Tomorrow is the Cabinet meeting; I will—the senior ministers will be there, my colleagues will be there, I will bring it up.
I will take the bold step of presenting this as a recommendation from Parliament, from Muar."
Najib would serve his house arrest until August 2028, accounting for some two years of his reduced six-year jail sentence for his convictions in the SRC International case.
The former prime minister was also convicted on multiple counts of corruption and money laundering in the 1MDB case.
Najib's lawyers had indicated they would appeal.

Title: Melaka polls: Pakatan pledges to abolish seven appointed assemblymen seats if elected
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 12 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) has pledged to repeal the state legislation allowing the appointment of seven Melaka state assembly members if it wins the mandate to govern the state in the 16th Melaka election.
Melaka PH chairman Adly Zahari said savings from abolishing the appointed seats would be channelled towards homeownership assistance for young people and programmes to develop young entrepreneurs.
He said the proposal was among the coalition’s pledges under its Aspirasi Melaka Rumah Kita manifesto, which focuses on addressing the needs of residents, particularly the younger generation.
“The provision allowing seven appointed assembly members was approved by the State Legislative Assembly under the previous Barisan Nasional administration.
“If the people of Melaka give PH the mandate, we will abolish these seven appointed seats,” he told a daily press conference at the PH operations centre in Bukit Baru today.
Adly said PH also planned to reopen the Chief Minister’s official residence at Seri Bendahara for regular meet-the-people sessions if it returned to power.
He said the initiative, introduced during PH’s administration in 2018, would allow residents to raise concerns directly with the state’s top leadership and seek solutions.
“We held these sessions every Friday when PH governed Melaka, and many of the issues raised could be resolved through direct engagement between residents and state leaders,” he said.
Meanwhile, Adly, who is also PH’s candidate for the Bukit Katil state seat, urged voters to support the coalition’s candidates contesting 24 of the 28 seats in the state election.
He said PH wanted the opportunity to demonstrate its ability to represent constituents, address local concerns and implement its election pledges.
“Give us the opportunity to serve in the Melaka State Assembly. We want to prove our capabilities through constituency work, legislative action and policies that deliver on our pledges. Your vote is a trust we will not squander,” he said.
Adly also urged Melaka voters living outside the state to plan their journeys home ahead of polling this Saturday.
He encouraged local voters to cast their ballots early, preferably in the morning, as rain was common in the afternoon.
For the latest news on the state polls, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/. — Bernama

Title: Four men convicted in Wang Kelian mass graves case repatriated to Thailand
Article:
KANGAR, Nov 12 — Six Thai nationals, including four convicted in a case linked to migrant smuggling camps and the discovery of mass graves in Wang Kelian in 2015, were repatriated to Thailand yesterday after completing their prison sentences in Malaysia.
Perlis Immigration director Mohammad A’sim Md Ali said the four men, aged between 31 and 61, were extradited from Thailand to Malaysia in June 2023 to face legal proceedings.
He said the Kangar High Court sentenced them to five years’ imprisonment on January 7 this year after they pleaded guilty to charges under Section 26H of the Anti-Trafficking in Persons and Anti-Smuggling of Migrants Act (Atipsom) 2007 for harbouring smuggled migrants.
Mohammad A’sim said the court ordered their sentences to run from June 22, 2023, the date of their arrest.
“Two other Thai nationals, aged 32 and 38, who were also repatriated, had completed their sentences for separate immigration offences under Sections 8(3)(a) and 15(4) of the Immigration Act 1959/63. Neither was involved in the Atipsom case,” he said in a statement.
Mohammad A’sim said all six men were handed over to Thai authorities at the Wang Kelian Immigration Post near Padang Besar for further action in accordance with Thailand’s legal procedures.
“The repatriation was coordinated between the authorities of both countries to ensure an orderly handover. The Perlis Immigration Department appreciates the close cooperation and strategic ties established with the Thai authorities,” he said. — Bernama
